t: God Gave Up His Own Son
v: He who didn’t spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?
b: This passage shows us God's unmatched love and sacrifice. He did not hesitate to give up His own only Son, Jesus Christ, to save us. Such love is without doubt the greatest and most selfless. Since God was willing to give up for us what was most precious to Him, would He not also give us everything we need?

It is like a wealthy father who, to rescue a child in trouble, is willing to give up all his wealth, even selling his beloved house. This father's love and sacrifice are beyond compare; he is willing to pay everything for this child. In the same way, God gave up His Son to save us, a love far beyond what we humans can understand.

A mother named Tianli had a son who suffered a serious car accident and needed a huge sum for surgery. Tianli was not wealthy, but she resolved to do everything she could to save her son. She sold her house and all her property, and even quit her job to care for her son with her whole heart. This mother's love moved countless people and drew attention and help from all sectors of society, and in the end her son recovered miraculously. Tianli's love and sacrifice let us see the most selfless devotion a mother can give for her child.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from this passage and story how deep and selfless God's love for us is. He not only gave up Jesus for us but also promised to give us everything we need. Let us be thankful, commit ourselves to God, trust in His provision and leading, and learn to treat the people around us with the same love and sacrifice.
ah: In Romans 8:32, the apostle Paul reminds us that He who did not spare His own Son but delivered Him up for us all, how will He not also with Him freely give us all things? This verse shows God's selfless love: He gave up His only Son, Jesus Christ, to save the world. Today, how should we practice this spirit of self-denial in daily life? Here are some specific ways to help us put this verse into practice in daily life:
a: Think of others
In daily life, learn to look at problems from others' point of view, care about their needs, and help them within the limits of your ability.
Give your time and energy

Self-denial is not only material help but also giving our time and energy. Volunteering, caring for lonely elderly people, and tutoring children with learning difficulties are all concrete actions in which we can practice the spirit of self-denial.
Tolerance and forgiveness
In getting along with others, learn tolerance and forgiveness, and lay down your own prejudices and resentments. This builds harmonious relationships better.
Give and share
Of the resources we have, learn to share and give to help those in difficulty. Whether money, food or other supplies, this is a concrete expression of self-denial.
Pass on love and care
Pass on God's love and care by practical action, letting our lives become a channel that witnesses to God's love and influences and changes those around us.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You did not spare Your own Son but delivered Him up for us all. Give us hearts of self-denial, so that in daily life we can think of others, give our time and energy, learn tolerance and forgiveness, and be willing to share our resources. Help us pass on Your love through practical action, and let our lives be Your witness, glorifying Your name. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find satisfaction in God's love and provision, and respond to His great love with a thankful heart. Amen!

v: No one takes it away from me, but I lay it down by myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. I received this commandment from my Father.”
b: This passage shows the sovereignty of Jesus Christ and His great love in willingly laying down His life for us. Jesus emphasizes that His life was not forcibly taken but laid down by Himself voluntarily. This is a love and obedience of the greatest degree, embodying His complete submission to the Father.

It is like a brave firefighter who, facing a raging fire, rushes into the blaze without regard for his own life to rescue those trapped. The firefighter's action is not because he is forced but out of love for life and faithfulness to duty. In the same way, Jesus Christ voluntarily laid down His life; this love and sacrifice goes beyond the scope of what we humans can understand.

A man named Mark was a doctor. One day he received news that a serious epidemic had broken out in a remote village and medical help was needed. Mark knew that going there meant running a great risk of infection, but he still decided to go voluntarily. He brought not only medical equipment and medicine but also cared for the patients with his whole heart, and in the end saved countless lives. Mark's selfless devotion and spirit of self-denial moved the whole village and let them see the power of love.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the example of Jesus and the story of Mark that true love is being willing to give oneself for others. Jesus voluntarily laid down His life to save us and give us eternal life. Let us also be willing, in life, for the sake of loving others, to deny ourselves and give, showing Christ's love.
ah: John 10:18 emphasizes Jesus' sovereignty and His love in voluntarily laying down His life, which is the highest example of selfless self-denial. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Take up responsibility proactively
In the family, at work and in the church, take up responsibility proactively and serve others, instead of passively waiting for others to ask.
Sacrifice your own interests
Learn to sacrifice your own time, money and comfort when needed to help those who need help. Such actions can show Christ's love and selfless spirit.
Act in love
Like Jesus, love and care for others selflessly, especially those in difficulty and need, whether friends, family or strangers.
Hold to the principles of faith
When facing challenges and temptations, hold to the principles of faith, even if it means taking risks or facing difficulty. This persistence shows our loyalty and obedience to God.
Share the love of Jesus
Actively share the gospel message that Jesus laid down His life for us, so that more people know and experience His love and salvation. This is the highest expression of our self-denial.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Jesus' example how to deny ourselves selflessly. Give us courage and strength, so that in daily life we can take up responsibility proactively, sacrifice our own interests, and act in love. Help us hold to the principles of faith and actively share the love of Jesus, so that more people know and experience His salvation. May our lives glorify Your name. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain strength in Jesus' love, learn self-denial, and be a blessing to others. Amen!

v: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her,
b: This passage emphasizes how a husband should love his wife: this love should be like Christ's love for the church, a selfless love that gives itself up. Christ willingly laid down His life for the church, which is the highest expression of love. A husband's love for his wife should also have this spirit of unconditional devotion and sacrifice.

It is like a captain who holds his post in a storm, regardless of his own safety, doing his utmost to protect the passengers and crew. Even in the face of huge waves, he does not abandon them, making sure everyone arrives safely at the destination. This captain's selflessness and devotion is just like Christ's love for the church.

A husband named Wayne had been married to his wife for many years, and they were deeply devoted. One day his wife was unfortunately diagnosed with a serious illness, needing long-term treatment and care. Wayne did not hesitate for a moment; he quit his job and stayed at home to focus on caring for his wife. Every day he cooked for her, helped her with rehabilitation, and stayed by her side, giving her encouragement and support. Wayne's love and devotion moved many people, who saw a concrete display of Christlike love between husband and wife.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the example of Christ and the story of Wayne that true love is being willing to give oneself for others. As husbands, we should love our wives as Christ loved the church, willing to give ourselves up for them, with unconditional devotion and sacrifice. Let us practice this love in life, so that our marriages and families may be filled with Christ's love and grace.
ah: In Ephesians 5:25, the apostle Paul teaches husbands to love their wives, even as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for it. This verse reminds us that whether in the family or the church, we should learn Christ's selflessness and spirit of sacrifice. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Unconditional love
In the family and in social settings, follow Christ's example and show unconditional love to others, without counting the return.
Put others' needs first
In making decisions and taking action, first consider the needs of family, church members and friends, lay down self, and meet the needs of others.
Continual care and concern
In the family, especially as a husband, continually care for and look after your wife, showing love not only in big things but also in the details of daily life.
Willingness to sacrifice
Following the example of Christ, be willing to sacrifice your time, energy and resources for the benefit of family, church and others, embodying the spirit of self-denial.
Build a healthy spiritual life
Keep an intimate relationship with God, and through prayer, Bible reading and devotions keep renewing yourself, letting God's love fill us so that we can love others better.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching to love others selflessly as Christ loved the church. Give us strength, so that in daily life we can love others unconditionally, put others' needs first, continually care for and look after our families and church members, and be willing to sacrifice for them. Help us build a healthy spiritual life, so that Your love fills us and is passed on through us to more people. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain strength in Christ's love, learn self-denial, and be a blessing to your family. Amen!

v: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
b: This passage shows Paul's profound experience of faith. His being crucified with Christ means that his past sin and old self have died, and now it is Christ who lives in him. This new life comes through believing in Jesus, because the Son of God loved us and gave Himself up for us.

It is like a tree that withers through the cold winter, then sprouts again when spring comes and blossoms into new life. Christ's self-giving and resurrection have given us new life, letting us live in Him abundantly and meaningfully.

A woman named Sarah went through many setbacks and failures in her youth, and her life was for a time in despair. One day, in church, she heard the pastor speak of Christ's self-giving and love. She was deeply moved and decided to receive Christ, and began a new life. Sarah took an active part in the church's ministry and kept helping those in need, and her life became full of joy and peace. She understood that the one who now lives is no longer the failed self of the past, but Christ living in her, giving her strength and hope.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the experience of Paul and Sarah, receive Christ's self-giving and love, and let Christ live in us. Our lives are changed by His love; they are no longer what they were, but have new hope and direction. Let us live out this new life with faith and love, influencing and blessing those around us.
ah: In Galatians 2:20, the apostle Paul teaches us that Christ, because He loved us, gave Himself up for us, and now it is no longer we who live but Christ who lives in us. We are to live out such a life in our daily lives. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching:
a: Remember Christ's sacrifice every day
Take time every day to meditate on Christ's self-giving love for us, which will inspire us to treat others with the same love and spirit of sacrifice.
Let Christ live in us
Let Christ's love and teaching, through the Holy Spirit, guide our conduct and decisions. Whether in treating family, friends or strangers, show the character of Christ.
Trust in the Son of God
Whatever challenges and difficulties we face, trust firmly in the Son of God, Jesus Christ, because He loved us and gave Himself up for us.
Practice love and sacrifice
In daily life, learn to sacrifice time, energy and resources for others, especially those who need help and support.
Take part in church ministry
Take an active part in the church's various ministries and activities, expressing our love for and obedience to Christ through practical action, and growing in service.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching of Christ's self-giving love for us. Help us remember Christ's sacrifice every day, let Christ live in us, and trust in Him in life. Help us practice the spirit of love and sacrifice, take an active part in the church's ministry, and express our love for You through action. May our lives glorify Your name and become a witness to Your love. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain new life and strength in Christ's love and self-giving, and live out the abundant life He has in you. Amen!

v: Walk in love, even as Christ also loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet-smelling fragrance.
b: This passage teaches us to walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us, becoming a sacrifice that pleases God. Christ's love and sacrifice set the highest example for us, and we too should imitate Him, living each day with a spirit of love and devotion.

It is like a candle, which burns itself to light others. A candle's value lies in its burning and its light; it is willing to give itself up so that people in the dark may have light and warmth. In the same way, we should be like this candle, serving others with love and sacrifice, so that our lives become a blessing to others.

A nurse named Lisa worked in the emergency room of a hospital. Every day she faced all kinds of emergencies, the suffering of patients and the anxiety of their families. Though the work pressure was great and the hours long, Lisa always treated every patient with love and patience. She not only provided medical care but often offered comfort and encouragement. Once a critically ill patient said to Lisa, “You are like an angel, bringing me hope and strength.” Lisa's love and devotion not only healed patients' bodies but also warmed their hearts.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the example of Christ and the story of Lisa, and act with love and devotion. Our love and sacrifice, though small, are a sweet-smelling offering in God's eyes, able to bring hope and blessing to others. Let us practice this love in life, become vessels of God, and glorify His name.
ah: In Ephesians 5:2, the apostle Paul teaches us to walk in love, as Christ gave Himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet-smelling aroma. This verse reminds us to practice Christ's love and spirit of sacrifice in daily life. Here are some specific ways to help us put this teaching into practice:
a: Treat others with love
In daily life, treat everyone around you with love, whether family, friends or strangers. Love should be the motive for our actions.
Sacrifice self
Following Christ's example, be willing to sacrifice your time, energy and resources for the good of others. This shows our love for God and for others.
Serve others
Take an active part in service in the church and community, helping those in need through practical action. This is a concrete expression of self-denial.
Persist in love in difficulty
Even when facing challenges and difficulty, persist in acting in love, because such love and sacrifice is a sweet-smelling offering in God's eyes.
Daily devotions
Keep an intimate relationship with God, and through prayer, Bible reading and devotions keep renewing yourself, letting God's love fill us so that we can love others better.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching to walk in love, giving ourselves up as Christ did, to be a sweet-smelling offering. Help us treat others with love in daily life, be willing to sacrifice self, actively serve others, and persist in love in difficulty. Help us keep daily devotions and an intimate relationship with You, so that our lives may be a sacrifice that pleases You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's presence in love and devotion, and be a blessing and light to others. Amen!

v: who gave himself as a ransom for all, the testimony at the proper time,
b: This passage emphasizes that Jesus Christ gave Himself for us, becoming the ransom for all, redeeming us from sin. This is God's immeasurable love and grace for humanity. Jesus Christ's sacrifice has not only brought us redemption but also shown His boundless love.

It is like a firefighter who, regardless of his own safety, rushes into a burning building and rescues those trapped. His spirit of sacrifice saves the lives of many and gives them a new life. Christ's self-giving is the same: He paid the greatest price for us so that we could be born again.

A man named Weichen lost his way in his youth and fell into the abyss of drugs and crime. Weichen's family and friends despaired for him, but they kept praying for him and gave him unconditional love and support. Finally, at a church meeting, Weichen heard the story of Jesus giving Himself for him. He was deeply moved and decided to repent and change his life, and succeeded in quitting drugs at a gospel rehabilitation center. Afterward he began to take an active part in church activities and helped others at the rehabilitation center break free from the bondage of drugs. Weichen's life was completely changed by Christ's love and self-giving, and he has now become an example and a symbol of hope to many.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the example of Christ and the story of Weichen, and receive the great love of Jesus Christ who gave Himself for us. He laid down His life for us so that we could gain freedom and new life. We should also, with the same love and spirit of self-denial, love others and help them find hope and direction in life.
ah: In 1 Timothy 2:6, the apostle Paul teaches us that Christ gave Himself as a ransom for all, and that this testimony will be proved in its own time. This verse reminds us that Christ's spirit of self-giving was to save us, and calls us to practice this selfless love in life. Here are some specific ways to help us put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Giving in love
In the family and in social settings, follow Christ's example, loving and caring for others selflessly without counting the return, showing Christ's love in both words and actions.
Giving up time

Be willing to give your time to people in need, whether visiting the sick, caring for orphans and widows, or taking part in community service, showing through action our response to Christ's spirit of self-giving.
Sharing resources
Learn to share your resources; money, supplies or skills can all be used to help those in difficulty. This is a concrete expression of Christ's spirit of self-giving.
Patience and tolerance

In getting along with others, learn patience and tolerance. Even in the face of challenges and misunderstanding, use Christ's love to embrace and accept others. This is another expression of self-denial.
Actively spread the gospel
Spread the gospel of Christ with our words and conduct, helping more people know Jesus and experience His love and salvation. This is the best response to Christ's spirit of self-giving.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching that Christ gave Himself as a ransom for all. Help us give in love, give up our time, and share our resources in daily life, and be patient and tolerant in our relationships. Help us actively spread the gospel, so that more people know Jesus and experience His love and salvation. May our lives be a witness to Your love. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain strength and hope in Christ's love and redemption, live out His love, and be a blessing to others. Amen!

v: who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.
b: This passage reveals the purpose of Jesus Christ's self-giving for us: He not only redeemed us from sin but also purified us, making us His chosen people, zealous for good works. This is the core of the Christian life: we receive new life because of Christ's self-giving, and are called to do good and glorify God.

It is like a gardener who not only clears the weeds in the garden but also plants beautiful flowers and tends them carefully so that the garden becomes beautiful and prosperous. Christ's self-giving for us cleared the sin out of our lives and planted seeds of goodness and love, so that our lives may blossom into beautiful fruit.

A teacher named Kate taught at a school in a poor area. Most of the students there came from broken families, lacked love and care, and had poor grades. Kate saw the despair in these children's hearts and decided to change their lives with her love and patience. She not only taught carefully in class but also offered tutoring and care after class. She organized extracurricular activities, took the children to visit museums, and taught them basic values for life.

One day, a student with many problems, Tom, began to change gradually with Kate's help. His grades improved significantly, and he became more confident and cheerful. Tom said gratefully to Kate, “Teacher, you changed my life and let me see hope.” Kate's love and devotion were like Christ's self-giving, renewing and changing the lives of these children.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the example of Christ and the story of Kate, and receive the great love of Jesus Christ who gave Himself for us. He laid down His life for us so that we would be redeemed from all iniquity, and called us to do good and be His witnesses. Let us practice this love and these good deeds in life, and glorify God's name.
ah: In Titus 2:14, the apostle Paul teaches us that Christ gave Himself for us, redeeming us from all iniquity and purifying us to be a people for His own possession, zealous for good works. This verse reminds us that Christ's self-giving was not only to redeem us but also to have us live a pure life zealous for good works. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Confess and repent
Examine yourself every day, confess sin to God, and ask for His forgiveness and cleansing. Only when our hearts are clean can we do good better for the Lord.
Keep a life of devotions
Through prayer and Bible reading, keep an intimate relationship with God, letting God's Word guide our conduct and decisions.
Actively do good
In the family, at work or in the community, actively look for opportunities to do good and help those in need, showing Christ's love and spirit of self-denial.
Refuse the enticement of sin
In daily life, stay alert at all times, refuse the enticement of sin, and keep walking on God's right path.
Be a witness
Be a witness of Christ by our words and conduct, influencing and inspiring those around us, letting them see the beautiful character and selfless love of a Christian.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching that Christ gave Himself for us and redeemed us from all iniquity. Help us confess and repent every day, keep a life of devotions, actively do good, and refuse the enticement of sin. Let our lives be Your witness, influencing and inspiring more people to walk on Your right path. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain strength and hope in Christ's love and redemption, be freed from sin, be zealous for good works, and be a blessing to others. Amen!

v: who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us out of this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father—
b: This passage tells us that Christ gave Himself for our sins, according to the will of God, in order to rescue us from this present evil age. It reminds us that Christ's sacrifice was not only for personal redemption but so that in this world full of sin we might find light and hope.

It is like a brave doctor who, when an epidemic is raging, risks his life to go to the stricken area, treating patients and bringing hope of healing. This doctor's sacrifice and devotion saves the lives of many and restores their health and hope. In the same way, Christ's self-giving was so that we might find redemption and new life in a world of sin.

A young woman named Anna met many temptations and challenges as she grew up and gradually became lost in the sin of this age. One day she attended a Christian summer camp and heard a preacher speak of the love and sacrifice of Christ's self-giving for us. Anna was deeply moved and decided to repent and receive Christ as her Savior. She began to take an active part in church activities and to bear witness to Christ's love and power at her school and in her community. Anna's life was completely changed by Christ's self-giving; she was rescued from sin and became an inspiration and example to many.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the example of Christ and the story of Anna, and receive the great love of Jesus Christ who gave Himself for us. He laid down His life for us to deliver us from this evil age, and called us to do good and be His witnesses. Let us practice this love and these good deeds in life, and glorify God's name.
ah: In Galatians 1:4, the apostle Paul teaches us that Christ gave Himself for our sins, according to the will of our God and Father, to deliver us out of this present evil age. This verse reminds us that Christ's self-giving was to save us, so that we may be delivered from this world full of sin. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Persist in daily devotions
Take time every day to read the Bible and pray, keep an intimate relationship with God, and let God's Word become the guide of our lives, helping us tell good from evil.
Choose a holy life
Make the right choices in life, reject any conduct that does not accord with God's will, and keep a pure heart and behavior.
Cultivate spiritual discernment
Learn to discern what is of God and what is a temptation of this age, and rely on the guidance of the Holy Spirit to choose to follow God's way.
Take an active part in church life
Take an active part in the church's gatherings and ministries, grow together with brothers and sisters, and encourage and support one another, strengthening our spiritual resilience in this age.
Influence others with Christ's love
Influence those around us with our words and conduct, passing on Christ's love and truth to them, helping them know God's salvation and stay away from this evil age.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching that Christ gave Himself for us to deliver us from this evil age. Help us persist in daily devotions, choose a holy life, cultivate spiritual discernment, and take an active part in church life. Let us influence others with Christ's love and lead more people to know You and be freed from the bondage of sin. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain strength and hope in Christ's love and redemption, be free from sin, live in the light, and be a blessing to others. Amen!

t: Deny Yourself and Take Up the Cross
v: He said to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
b: This passage emphasizes the cost and demands of following Jesus. Jesus tells us that to truly follow Him, we must deny ourselves and take up our cross daily, which means we must lay down our own wishes and desires and fully submit to God's will.

It is like a mountain climber who, in order to reach the beautiful view at the summit, must put down his heavy pack, take only the necessary equipment, and focus on each step of the climb. The Christian life is the same: we need to put down the burdens that keep us from drawing near to God, take up the cross every day, and walk on the road of following Jesus.

A young man named Mike used to live a life pursuing fame and pleasure, but felt empty inside. One day he attended a church retreat and heard the pastor speak of Jesus' self-giving and the cost of following Him. Mike was deeply moved and decided to change his life. He gave up a high-paying job and chose to join a non-profit organization dedicated to helping children in poor areas receive an education. Mike's family and friends were surprised by his choice, but he said firmly, “Following Jesus is the most important decision of my life. I am willing to deny myself, take up the cross, and live a real life for His love.”

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from the teaching of Jesus and the story of Mike, and accept the call to deny ourselves and take up the cross. Following Jesus is not an easy road, but it is the only road that leads to eternal life and true fulfillment. Let us take up our cross every day, walk in the light of Christ, and be His witnesses.
ah: In Luke 9:23, Jesus teaches us that to follow Him we must deny ourselves and take up our cross daily. This verse emphasizes the cost of and commitment to following Christ. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Daily devotions
Take time every day to read the Bible and pray, build an intimate relationship with God, seek His guidance, and let His Word become the strength of our lives.
Put God's will first
In making decisions and taking action, first consider God's will, be willing to lay down your own plans and desires, and submit to God's leading.
Bear responsibility and challenge
In the family, at work or in the church, take on responsibility proactively, do not shrink back when facing challenge and difficulty, hold to your faith, and take up your own cross.
Love and serve others
Learn from Jesus' example, loving and serving others selflessly, especially those in need, showing Christ's love and spirit of sacrifice.
Self-examination and repentance
Reflect regularly on your words and conduct, confess and repent, and ask God to cleanse our hearts and make us more like Christ.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Jesus' teaching that to follow Him we must deny ourselves and take up our cross daily. Help us keep daily devotions, put Your will first, boldly take on responsibility and challenge, and love and serve others selflessly. Please cleanse our hearts and make us more like Christ, a witness to Your love. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain strength and courage on the road of self-denial and following Jesus, live out His love, and be a blessing to others. Amen!

t: Deny Yourself and Follow the Lord
v: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
b: This passage makes it plain that following Jesus requires us to deny ourselves and take up our own cross. It means setting self aside, giving up our own desires and goals, and following Jesus wholeheartedly, accepting His guidance and His mission.

Think of a sailor who decides to set out on a long voyage into unknown waters. He must give up the comfort and safety of land and face storms and unseen dangers. His determination and courage allow him to discover new lands and open up a new world. In the same way, the Christian life is an adventure. We must lay down self and follow Jesus bravely, to explore and fulfill God’s plan for our lives.

There was a girl named Emily who loved music from childhood and dreamed of becoming a famous pianist. Her talent and hard work won her prize after prize in competitions, and her future looked bright. But as she was preparing for an important international competition, she learned that an orphanage in her hometown was in urgent need. The children lacked basic necessities and educational resources. Emily faced a difficult choice: keep pursuing her dream, or give up the competition and help these orphans?

Emily thought deeply about Jesus’ teaching and decided to deny herself and take up her cross. She cancelled her plans for the competition, went home, and used her musical gifts to raise funds so the orphanage would have what it needed. She also went regularly to teach the children music, bringing them hope and joy. Emily’s decision not only changed the lives of those orphans, but also gave her a deeper sense of fulfillment and meaning.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from Jesus’ teaching and Emily’s story, and accept the call to deny ourselves and take up the cross. Following Jesus takes courage and resolve, but it is the road to true fulfillment and eternal life. Let us take up our cross every day, walk in the light of Christ, and become His witnesses.
ah: In Matthew chapter 16, verse 24, Jesus said to His disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.” This verse reminds us that following Jesus means laying down self and shouldering our responsibilities and challenges every day. Here are some practical ways to put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Connect with God every day
Set aside time each day to read the Bible and pray, seeking God’s guidance, and let His Word become the strength and direction of our lives.
Put others’ needs first
In daily life, learn to deny yourself and put others’ needs first, being willing to give up some of your own comfort for the happiness and well-being of others.
Take responsibility
Whether in the family, at work, or in the church, take on your responsibilities willingly and do your best, in matters great and small.
Persevere in hardship
When you face difficulties and challenges, do not shrink back. Hold on to your faith, take up your cross, and trust God’s strength to help you overcome.
Be a blessing to others
Care for and help others with love and action, whether through giving, serving, or simple acts of concern, so that our lives become a blessing to others.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Jesus’ teaching to deny ourselves and take up our cross to follow Him. Help us to connect with You every day, put others’ needs first, take responsibility, persevere in hardship, and be a blessing to others. May our lives bring glory to You and influence and encourage many more to walk in Your ways. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive strength and courage on the road of self-denial and following Jesus, live out His love, and be a blessing to others. Amen!

v: The LORD’s voice is on the waters. The God of glory thunders, even the LORD on many waters.
b: In this verse we witness God’s incomparable glory and His majesty in the natural world. What is described here is not merely a natural phenomenon but a display of God’s glory, reminding us that He is the almighty Creator.

Like a sudden storm whose power cannot be ignored, this picture helps us understand the voice of God’s glory. Whether thunder or lightning, each is a display of His power, teaching us to honor Him and to stand in awe of His greatness.

Think of a climber standing on a mountain peak for the first time, looking out over the view below. The awe and wonder he feels is a taste of God’s glory. It reminds us that whenever we feel the grandeur of nature, we are in fact experiencing the glory of God.

We should bring the truth of this passage into our lives, seeing God’s glory not only in experiences of nature but also looking for His guidance and glory in every detail of daily life. When we face difficulty or pressure, let us remember that just as God commands the thunder, He also holds our lives in His hands.
ah: Psalm 29, verse 3, reminds us of God’s majesty and glory. He rules over heaven and earth and all things, and His power is beyond compare. Here are some practical ways to put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Revere God
In prayer and worship each day, remember God’s greatness and majesty, keep your heart in awe of Him, and come before Him with humility.
Listen for God’s voice
In Bible reading and devotions, learn to be still and listen to God’s voice, and let His Word guide your life and decisions.
Give thanks and praise
In good times and in bad, learn to give thanks and praise to God, for His glory and grace are everywhere, and His power can help us overcome every difficulty.
Bear witness to God’s glory
Witness to God’s glory by the way you speak and act, so that those around you see the change and blessing in your life and come to know God’s greatness and love.
Depend on God’s strength
When you face challenges and difficulties, do not rely on your own strength but on God’s, for His voice is over the many waters and His power can help you overcome every difficulty.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Psalm 29:3 that You are the God of glory, that Your voice is on the waters, and that You rule over all. Help us to revere You every day, listen to Your voice, give thanks and praise, and witness to Your glory with our lives. When we face challenges, may we rely on Your strength and experience Your mighty power. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May we all see God’s glory in our lives and glorify Him in everything we do. Amen!

v: Who is the King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.
b: This verse brings us great comfort and encouragement. It reminds us that God is our King of glory, full of strength and power. Whatever challenge or difficulty we face, He is at our side, fighting for us.
Like a brave general protecting his people on the battlefield, our God does the same. When we face battles and trials in life, remember that God’s strength and power can carry us through.

A brother named Jiancheng once shared his testimony. He faced a difficulty that seemed impossible to overcome: his business was on the verge of bankruptcy, and he had fallen into deep despair. But in his most helpless moment, he remembered this verse and recalled that God is the King of glory, Yahweh strong and mighty. He began to pray every day, entrusted his troubles to God, and firmly believed that God would open a way for him. Sure enough, a miracle happened. His business not only survived but found new opportunities and growth. He is convinced that all of this was God’s work in his life, and that God’s glory was revealed in his hardship.

Dear family, whatever challenges and trials we face, let us remember that God is our King of glory. He is strong and mighty, and He will surely lead us through every difficulty. If we trust in Him, He will surely show His power and glory.
ah: Psalm 24, verse 8, reminds us that the LORD is our King of glory, with boundless strength and power, especially when we face the battlefields of life. Here are some practical ways to put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Depend on God’s strength
When you face challenges and difficulties, do not rely only on your own strength. Look to God, for He is strong and mighty, and in Him we can find true strength.
Faith and courage
Remember that the LORD is mighty in battle and can help us overcome every difficulty. So whatever challenge you face, have faith and courage, believing that God is with you and will give you victory.
Praise and thanksgiving

Come before God each day with a heart of praise and thanksgiving, thanking Him for His strength and protection and praising His greatness and glory. This will encourage us to keep a positive attitude in every circumstance.
Seek God’s guidance
Before making decisions and taking action, seek God’s guidance. He is a wise King, and His guidance can keep us on the right path so that we do not lose our way.
Work together with God
Align your work and life with God’s plan, and let His glory be shown in your life. In this way we can become His witnesses and influence many others.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Psalm 24:8 that You are the King of glory, Yahweh strong and mighty. Help us to rely on Your strength in the challenges of life, give us faith and courage, and let us come before You every day with hearts of praise and thanksgiving. Guide our decisions and actions, so that we may work together with You and Your glory may be shown in our lives. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you, in every difficult moment, look up to the King of glory, the LORD strong and mighty, who will surely fight for you and bring victory. Amen!

v: The LORD’s glory mounted up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the LORD’s glory.
b: This passage describes an extraordinarily magnificent scene: the glory of the LORD filling the whole temple, bringing light and an atmosphere of holiness. It symbolizes God’s presence, which is not only holy but full of power. We might compare this glory to a sunrise, when the first rays of the sun break across the sky and light up the whole land, bringing hope and a new beginning.

Imagine a painter trying to capture this moment on canvas, using bright colors to express the shining radiance. Such a painting would be not only a feast for the eyes but an encouragement to the soul. When we meet darkness or difficulty in life, recalling this picture reminds us that God’s glory and light are always around us, and His presence will guide us through any gloom.

So when we feel pressure or fear in daily life, let us remember the glory of the LORD. Just as radiance filled the temple, God’s presence can fill our hearts and every corner of our lives. We are called to experience this glory and to find peace and guidance in it.
ah: In Ezekiel chapter 10, verse 4, we read: “Yahweh’s glory went up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of Yahweh’s glory.” This verse reminds us that the LORD’s glory is everywhere, and His presence can fill our lives. Here are some practical ways to put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Draw near to God every day
Spend time each day reading the Bible, praying, and worshiping, letting God’s presence fill your soul, and sense His glory and power.
Witness for God in daily life
Show God’s glory in your words and actions, so that others see His love, grace, and truth through you.
Take an active part in church life
Join in the church’s worship, fellowship, and ministry, experiencing God’s presence together with your brothers and sisters, supporting and encouraging one another.
Reflect God’s glory
At home, at work, and in the community, strive to be light and salt, reflecting God’s glory through your actions.
Learn to give thanks and praise
In good times and in bad, keep a thankful heart and praise God’s greatness and goodness, so that your heart is filled with His glory.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through the book of Ezekiel that Your glory fills heaven and earth. Help us to draw near to You every day and let Your presence fill our lives. May we witness to Your glory in our lives, take an active part in church life, reflect Your radiance, and always keep hearts of thanksgiving and praise. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you sense the radiance of the LORD’s glory in every circumstance and find strength and comfort in His presence. Amen!

v: The appearance of the LORD’s glory was like devouring fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel.
b: This passage paints a magnificent picture: the glory of the LORD appearing on the mountaintop like a burning fire. The flame symbolizes not only God’s might and power to purify, but also His protection and guidance of His people. Like a campfire in the dark of night, it gives not only light and warmth but also a sense of safety in the cold and darkness.

Imagine someone lost in the wilderness. Night has fallen and everything around is pitch black, when suddenly a blaze of firelight appears in the distance. To that lost traveler the fire is not only a source of light but a sign of direction and hope. He walks toward the light, and not only finds his way home but feels warmth and comfort along the way.

This is the power of the LORD’s glory. On the journey of life, when we meet trouble and challenge and feel lost and afraid, the LORD’s glory is like that fire, lighting our path and bringing us hope and direction. We are called to walk toward this light, to place our lives under God’s glory and let His radiance shine on every step.
So when we face life’s pressures and an uncertain future, let us remember the glory of this flame and let it lead us forward. Wherever and whenever, God’s glory is our strength and our shield.
ah: In Exodus chapter 24, verse 17, we read: “The appearance of Yahweh’s glory was like devouring fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel.” This verse reminds us that the LORD’s glory is as intense and unmistakable as a consuming fire, and His presence and power are our guide and strength in life. Here are some practical ways to put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Keep a reverent heart
Always remember God’s greatness and glory, a power like a consuming fire, so that we keep our reverence for Him and walk humbly.
Daily devotions
Spend time each day reading the Bible, praying, and meditating, letting God’s Word kindle the flame of faith in our hearts and guide our words and actions.
Face challenges with courage
When you meet difficulties and challenges in life, do not shrink back. Remember that God’s glory is as mighty as a consuming fire, and He will surely give us courage and strength to overcome.
Witness for God in daily life
Through your words and actions, let others see what God is doing in your life, a testimony like a blazing fire that touches and inspires those around you.
Unity and mutual support
In the church and in the family, support one another with brothers and sisters, with a fiery enthusiasm that encourages everyone to grow together and witness to God’s glory.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through the book of Exodus that Your glory is as intense and unmistakable as a consuming fire. Help us to keep our reverence for You in daily life, to have daily devotions, to face challenges with courage, and to be witnesses to Your glory. May we support one another in unity in the church and in the family, and let Your glory be shown among us. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel God’s glory like a consuming fire in every season of life, and find strength and direction in the light of that glory. Amen!

v: As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the LORD’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke.
b: In this passage the prophet Ezekiel describes what he saw of the glory of the LORD. The picture is full of indescribable beauty and power, symbolizing God’s incomparable glory and majesty. Like the rainbow that appears in the sky after a storm, which fills us with wonder at the beauty of creation, this too is a display of God’s glory.

Imagine a photographer catching the moment a rainbow appears. It is not only a beautiful picture but a reminder that even after the storm, hope and goodness are waiting for us. That photographer’s picture, like the prophet Ezekiel’s vision, becomes a tool for bearing witness to God’s glory.

When we meet difficulty and challenge in life, let us remember the vision Ezekiel saw. Whether it is pressure at work, discord at home, or personal struggle, we can draw strength from this vision. When you feel crushed by the world, just look up at the rainbow, think of it as part of God’s glory, and you will find strength to go on.

Let us seek that likeness of glory through practical action, whether by serving others, caring for our families and friends, or contributing to our communities. Every small act of kindness can reflect God’s glory, just like a rainbow after rain, giving hope and light to those around us.
ah: In Ezekiel chapter 1, verse 28, we read: “As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness around it. This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke.” This verse reminds us that God’s glory is as beautiful and dazzling as a rainbow, and fills our lives. Here are some practical ways to put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Revere and honor God
Every day, keep reverence and honor for God in your life. As Ezekiel fell on his face when he saw the likeness of glory, let us humbly worship God and recognize His greatness.
Look for hope in hardship
Just as the rainbow appears after the rain, let us look for God’s hope and promises in hardship, trusting that He will bring light and goodness.
Witness to God’s glory
Witness to God’s glory by your words and actions, so that others see the radiance in your life and are drawn to God’s love and grace.
Keep a humble heart
No matter how great our achievements in life, stay humble and give the glory to God, recognizing that everything good is His gift.
Listen for God’s voice
In Bible reading and prayer, learn to listen for God’s voice and let His guidance be the compass of your life. Like Ezekiel, draw wisdom and strength from God’s Word.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through the book of Ezekiel that Your glory is as beautiful and dazzling as a rainbow. Help us to keep our reverence and honor for You in daily life, to look for hope in hardship, to witness to Your glory, to keep a humble heart, and to learn to listen for Your voice. May Your glory fill our lives and guide us forward. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. As you seek and reflect God’s glory, may you become a blessing and an encouragement to those around you. Amen!

v: Now therefore, our God, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
b: In daily life we are often busy pursuing our own reputation and achievements, and forget that the One truly worthy of praise is God’s name. Let me share a little story with you.

There was a young painter who dreamed of becoming a world-famous artist. He worked day and night and finally painted a stunning piece. At the exhibition his painting received the highest praise. Yet as people began to praise his talent, he felt a strange emptiness.

One day, while out for a walk, he met an old gardener who was pruning a beautiful tree. The young painter marveled, “You are a truly skilled gardener!” The old gardener smiled and said, “No, young man, I am only one of God’s little helpers. He created this tree and gave it life and beauty. All I do is help display His glory.”

This simple conversation opened the young painter’s eyes. He realized that his talent and achievements were all given by God. From that day on, he signed each of his paintings “For the glory of God” instead of his own name.

This story reminds us that every achievement and every step of progress in life should become a reason to praise God. When we succeed at work, let us not forget to thank the God who gave us the ability. When we admire the beauty of nature, let us remember to praise the Lord who created it all.

Let us learn to praise God often in daily life. When we get up in the morning, give thanks for a new day. At mealtimes, offer thanks for the food. When we face challenges, praise God for giving us strength to meet them. In this way our lives will become a song of ceaseless praise to God.

Dear family, let us practice together giving glory to God’s name. As we do, we will find our lives richer and our hearts more joyful. For praise is not only for God’s sake but for our own. It reminds us of God’s greatness and helps us keep humble and thankful hearts.
ah: 1 Chronicles 29:13 reminds us to thank God and praise His glorious name. This verse stresses the importance of worship and thanksgiving, and encourages us to remember God’s greatness at all times in daily life. Here are some practical ways to put it into practice:
a: Morning praise
Each day after you get up, spend five minutes praising God for His attributes, such as His lovingkindness, righteousness, and faithfulness. This habit helps us begin the day with the right attitude.
Gratitude journal
Each night before bed, write down at least three things from the day to be thankful for, big or small. This builds our ability to notice God’s grace.
Praise reminders
Set a daily reminder on your phone or computer to play a hymn or show a verse of praise at a certain time, so that we remember to praise God even when we are busy.
Sharing praise
At least once a week, share with family, friends, or group members what God has done in your life, and praise God together for it. This not only glorifies God but encourages one another.
Creative praise
Use your talents to praise God, such as writing poetry, drawing, composing music, or cooking. Offer your creation to God as praise for His glorious name.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You and praise Your glorious name. Help us in every day of our lives to remember Your greatness, to begin our days with morning praise, and to end each night with thankful hearts. Remind us to praise You even in our busyness, and to share Your works gladly with others. Give us creativity to use our talents to glorify You. May our lives be a continual praise to You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your life become a living sacrifice praising God’s glorious name, so that in praise you experience God’s presence and abundance. Amen!

v: As the livestock that go down into the valley, the LORD’s Spirit caused them to rest. So you led your people to make yourself a glorious name.
b: This verse reminds me of a little story. A young mountaineer was determined to climb a very challenging peak. He prepared well and set out full of confidence. But along the way he met unexpected difficulties: a blizzard, steep cliffs, and breathless high altitude.

Just when he was about to give up, he met an experienced guide. The guide not only showed him a safe route, but encouraged him when he was exhausted and gave him direction when he was confused. Under the guide’s leadership, the young man finally reached the summit and looked out over the magnificent valley. The experience not only fulfilled his dream but deeply changed his life.

This story is just what our passage describes. God is like that wise guide. He leads us through the hardships and dangers of life and brings us to a place of rest. The journey of our lives is full of challenges: a bottleneck in our career, trouble in relationships, or health problems. In such times we need to learn to trust God and listen to His guidance.

More importantly, the passage tells us that God leads us not only for our own good but to make a glorious name for Himself. When we experience God’s leading and protection in life and share these experiences with others, we are bearing witness to God and showing His glory.

Let us learn to seek God’s guidance in daily life. Whether making an honest decision at work or showing selfless love at home, we are adding glory to God’s name. When we experience His leading and blessing, let us courageously share it with others, so that more people come to know this God of glory.
ah: Isaiah 63:14 reminds us that God leads us and gives us rest, in order to make a glorious name for Himself. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Morning stillness
Each morning after you get up, spend ten minutes quietly before God, seeking His guidance and preparing for the day.
Rest reminders
Set three daily reminders on your phone to pause your work, take a deep breath, recall God’s presence, and enjoy a moment of rest.
Guidance journal
Each night before bed, review the day and record at least one thing in which you sensed God’s leading, to grow more sensitive to His work.
Sharing His glory
At least once a week, share on social media or with friends how God has shown His glory in your life, encouraging others to see what God is doing.
Serve others
Plan one concrete act of service each week, such as visiting a neighbor or helping a coworker, showing God’s love through action and making His name glorious.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us rest and guidance. Help us to be quiet before You every morning and listen to Your voice. Let us experience Your presence even in our busyness and enjoy true rest. Open our eyes so that we can see Your guidance in daily life. Give us courage and wisdom to share Your glory with others. Use our service to help more people know You and experience Your love. May our lives be vessels that make Your name glorious. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel God’s guidance in every stage of life, as if led down into a valley of rest. May your life be a witness to God’s glory, and may His name be lifted high through your faith and obedience. Amen!

v: Let the LORD’s glory endure forever. Let the LORD rejoice in his works.
b: Imagine we are standing on a mountaintop, gazing out across the wide sky. Sunlight falls on the green forests, clouds drift slowly through the blue, and a distant lake reflects the sky like a mirror. This magnificent sight cannot help but make us marvel at the greatness of the Creator.
Whenever we enjoy the beauty of nature, we can sense God’s glory. But God’s glory exists not only in the natural world; it is also in each of our lives.

Let me tell you a little story. A gardener named John took care of a beautiful garden. Every day he tended each plant with care, watering, fertilizing, and pruning. Gradually the garden became the loveliest place in town, and many people came to visit.

One day a visitor asked John, “Why do you take such trouble over these plants?” John smiled and answered, “Because I know every flower and every leaf was created by God. When I care for them, I am taking part in God’s creation, letting His glory bloom in this world.”
This story tells us that whatever we do can be an opportunity to show God’s glory. Perhaps we are not gardeners, but we can find our own “garden” in daily life.

Perhaps you are a teacher, teaching your students with love. Perhaps you are a doctor, healing patients with your skill. Perhaps you are a parent, raising your children with patience. Whatever our role, through our actions we can let God’s glory keep shining in this world.

When we admire God’s creation with thankful hearts, treat the people around us with love, and put passion into our work, we are letting God’s glory endure forever. Every good deed, every smile, and every act of helping another continues God’s creation and lets Him rejoice in His works.
Let us work together to show God’s glory in our lives, so that this world becomes a better place because we are in it.
ah: Psalm 104:31 reminds us that God’s glory is eternal, and that He rejoices in His own creation. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Praise creation
Spend time each day enjoying nature, whether the dawn, the sunset, or the flowers and trees, praising God’s wonderful creation and sensing His glory.
Gratitude journal
Each night record three things to be thankful for, cultivating a thankful heart and recognizing that our lives and everything we have are given by God.
Care for the environment
Show love for the world God created through everyday eco-friendly actions, such as saving water, reducing waste, and joining environmental activities.
Discover goodness
In daily life, watch especially for the good in the people and things around you and praise God for it, recognizing that it all reflects the glory of the Creator.
Share your joy
Share with others the glory and goodness of God you have discovered, encouraging them to see life with fresh eyes and praise God together.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we praise You, for Your glory endures forever. Open our eyes so that we may see Your wonderful creation in daily life. Help us always to keep thankful hearts and cherish all that You have given. Give us wisdom and strength to care for and steward this world better. May our lives reflect Your glory and share Your goodness with others. May our words and actions please You, as You rejoice in Your own works. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your life be a witness to God’s glory, and may His light shine from you on every road you walk. Amen!

v: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give to you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him,
b: Imagine you are standing before an enormous library that holds all the knowledge and wisdom in the world. You want to go in and explore, but you find the door locked. Suddenly a kindly elder comes up and hands you a key. The key not only opens the library door but helps you understand all the knowledge inside.
That elder is like our Heavenly Father, and the key is the spirit of wisdom and revelation He gives us.

A young man named Lihan had always been searching for the meaning of life. He read many books of philosophy and attended all kinds of lectures, but always felt something was missing. One day he decided to quiet himself and pray sincerely to God, asking Him for wisdom and revelation.

A wonderful thing happened. Lihan began to see God’s presence in his daily life. He felt God’s warmth in the sunshine, saw God’s creativity in the flowers, and sensed God’s love in his friends’ care. Gradually Lihan found he had a completely new understanding of life. He truly came to know God, and found direction for his life.

This story tells us that true wisdom and revelation come from our Heavenly Father. He is not only the Father of glory but a Father who longs for close fellowship with us. He desires that we truly know Him, not on the surface, but through deep, personal experience.

In our daily lives we too can seek this wisdom and revelation. When we face difficulties, we can stop and pray to our Heavenly Father. He will give us wisdom to make the right decisions. When we feel lost, we can be still and listen for God’s voice. He will give us revelation and show us the way forward.

Remember, our Heavenly Father is the Father of glory, and His wisdom far exceeds our imagination. When we come humbly before Him, He will give us the spirit of wisdom and revelation. This will help us know Him better, and also understand ourselves and this world better.

Let us come before our Heavenly Father every day and ask Him for wisdom and revelation. Let us observe the world around us with the eyes of the heart and look for God’s will in everything. As we do, we will come to know this Father of glory more and more, and our lives will be changed.
ah: Dear family, peace to you. Let us follow together today’s Soul Snack action guide: Ephesians 1:17 reminds us that God is the Father of glory, and that He gives us a spirit of wisdom and revelation so that we can truly know Him. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: 1. Deepen your devotions: Each day choose one verse, reflect deeply on the wisdom in it, and write down what God reveals to you personally. 2. Apply wisdom: In daily decisions, stop first and ask yourself, “Will this choice help me know God better?” 3. Share revelation: Each week share with a friend how God has revealed Himself to you, and encourage one another to grow. 4. Quiet listening: Set aside ten quiet minutes each day to listen closely for God’s voice and grow sensitive to His revelation. 5. Record thanks: Each night write down three things that show God’s wisdom, and know His glory more deeply with a thankful heart.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, Father of glory, we ask You to give us a spirit of wisdom and revelation to help us truly know You. May we understand Your Word more deeply in our devotions, seek Your guidance in our decisions, show Your works in our sharing, hear Your voice in the silence, and know Your glory in our thanksgiving. Make us witnesses to Your wisdom. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May the Father of glory give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation, so that you see His presence everywhere in life and know His love deeply. Amen!

v: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
b: On a pitch-dark night you are holding a bright lamp. The lamp lights your way, and brings light to those around you too. With every step you leave a trail of light in the darkness, guiding others forward. This is how we Christians ought to be: lights in the world.

A nurse named Mary worked in a busy hospital. Every day she faced a great many patients and heavy work. Yet Mary always kept a gentle smile and a patient attitude. She not only did her own work diligently, but often helped her colleagues and comforted her patients.

One day a patient asked her, “Mary, why are you always so happy and so loving?” Mary smiled and answered, “Because I believe in God’s love, and I hope that through my actions people can see God’s love.”
This simple answer deeply touched the patient, and it influenced many people in the hospital. Gradually more and more people took notice of Mary’s faith, and some even came to know God because of it.
Mary’s story is a living picture of today’s verse. Her good works were like a bright light shining before others, causing them to glorify the Father in heaven.

In our daily lives we too have countless opportunities to light the way for others. Perhaps it is doing our best at work, giving selfless love to family, or helping a stranger. These seemingly small actions can all become light for others.
But remember, the purpose of our shining is not to show off ourselves but to glorify God. Just as the moon reflects the light of the sun, our good works should reflect God’s love and grace.
Let us ask ourselves every day: What did I do today that glorifies God? Did the people around me see God’s love through my actions?
When we live this way, we become the light and salt of the world. Our lives become a living testimony, so that people come to know God through us and give glory to our Father in heaven.
Let us work together to let our light shine before others, not for our own reputation but for the glory of God. May our good works be lamps that guide others to God.
ah: Matthew 5:16 encourages us to be light and to give glory to the Father through our good works. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Good deeds journal
Each day record one good thing you did for someone else, big or small, to build the habit of doing good.
Anonymous help
Each week look for a chance to help someone anonymously, so that all the glory goes to God.
Thankful sharing
When you receive praise, learn to say “Thanks be to God,” giving the glory to the Father.
Open witness
Share on social media what God has done in your life, to draw others to know Him.
Character building
Each month focus on cultivating one Christian virtue (such as kindness, joy, or peace), and live out the likeness of Christ.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, help us to be lights in the world and to show Your glory through our good deeds each day. May we be glad to help others, know how to give praise to You, and be bold to share Your works. Shape our character so that our lives may draw more people to know You. May all the glory be Yours, our Father in heaven. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your life be like a bright lighthouse that lights up the darkness around you, so that people see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven. Amen!

t: The Father Glorified in the Son
v: Whatever you will ask in my name, I will do it, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
b: In this passage Jesus gives a deep and powerful promise: whatever we ask in His name, through faith and prayer, He will do. This is not only a promise to believers; it also reveals the relationship of glory between the Father and the Son.

Imagine a father and his child building a model airplane together. The child assembles each part following the father’s directions. When the plane is finally finished and flies successfully, the child’s success is also the glory of the father’s wisdom and guidance. This story is a miniature of our relationship with our Heavenly Father. When we ask for wisdom and help in Jesus’ name, and when those requests are granted, we witness not only the fulfillment of our own faith but also the glory of the Father.

This passage encourages us to pray boldly in Jesus’ name, whether for healing, wisdom, or reconciliation. Each answer is not only the satisfaction of what we asked but a declaration of our Father’s boundless glory. Through each prayer and each answer, we see the image of a loving, all-knowing, almighty God and Father, which strengthens our relationship with Him and encourages those around us.

So when you face difficulties, remember to bring your needs to the Father in Jesus’ name. Let our lives be a witness to His glory, not only because He answers us, but because through these answers our lives show the world His glory.
ah: John 14:13 reminds us that Jesus promises that whatever we ask in His name, He will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Persevere in prayer
In matters great and small, we should learn to pray in Jesus’ name and believe He will do what we ask, which displays God’s glory.
Act in faith
After praying, act in faith, believing that God will accomplish His will through our actions and that the Father will be glorified in the Son.
Share testimonies
Whenever God answers our prayers, share the testimony promptly, so that those around us see God’s works and glory.
Thanksgiving and worship
After each answered prayer, keep a thankful heart, worship God, and thank Him for His grace and faithfulness.
Glorify God’s name
In every area of life, strive to glorify God’s name, so that our words and actions reflect that we are disciples of Jesus Christ.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this passage, which reminds us to pray in Jesus’ name and to believe He will do what we ask, so that You are glorified in the Son. Help us to persevere in prayer, act in faith, share testimonies, worship with thanksgiving, and glorify Your name in our lives. May our lives be a witness to Your glory. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. As you call on the Father in Jesus’ name, may you experience His glory, and may that glory shine out through your life. Amen!

v: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.
b: In this passage Jesus stresses the importance of bearing spiritual fruit in a believer’s life. When our lives show the fruit of love, joy, peace, and more, it proves that we are His disciples and also brings glory to our Heavenly Father.

Imagine a gardener who carefully tends his orchard. When autumn comes and the trees bear abundant fruit, it is not only the result of the gardener’s hard work, but also leads everyone who sees it to praise the beauty and harvest of the orchard. In the same way, when our lives display Christian character, we are like fruit-bearing trees showing the world God’s work.

Here is an encouraging story about a businessman, well known in his industry for integrity and generosity. He not only succeeded in business but used his success to help people in need in society. His conduct led many people to respect and praise his faith, which was a display of the spiritual fruit in his life. His actions brought glory to God and inspired others to follow his example.

So each of us is called to bear good fruit in life, not only for the sake of our own spiritual growth, but so that our Heavenly Father may be glorified in this world. Let us actively seek and practice a way of life that makes us more like Christ, so that more people come to know God through our lives.
ah: John 15:8 reminds us that bearing much fruit glorifies the Father and proves that we are the Lord’s disciples. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Spiritual inventory
At the end of each week, reflect on your growth in faith, love, patience, and more; give thanks for progress and pray about your shortcomings.
Service plan
Each month set a concrete service goal, such as visiting the elderly or mentoring teenagers, and bear the fruit of your life in practical action.
Share your testimony
At least once a week, share with someone what God has done in your life, spreading the gospel and bearing the fruit of testimony.
Character building
Choose one fruit of the Spirit (such as love, joy, or peace) and practice it deliberately in daily life for a month.
Discipleship relationship
Build an accountable relationship with a spiritual elder or companion, sharing your growth regularly and encouraging each other to bear more fruit.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, help us to bear much fruit in our lives so that You are glorified. May we often reflect on our lives, serve others actively, and boldly share our testimonies. Shape our character so that we become more like Christ. Help us to support one another in our spiritual relationships and become true disciples. May our lives be a witness that glorifies You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you bear spiritual fruit in your life, so that the Father is glorified through you. Amen!

v: to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
b: This verse is Paul’s prayer in Ephesians, expressing a far-reaching desire: that God’s glory be displayed in the life of the church and its members. It reflects not only an understanding of God’s infinite glory but also a declaration of the church’s mission.

Imagine a lighthouse, a guide in the darkness. The church’s role in this world should be like a lighthouse too, leading people to Christ and lighting their way through the lives and witness of its members. Whenever we show God’s nature through acts of love, service, or grace, we display God’s glory in this world.

Here is a true story about a church leader who set up a community service program to inspire the members to take part in improving the community. They not only provided material aid but, through acts of care, carried Christ’s love into every corner, bringing help and hope to countless people. This not only increased the church’s influence in the community but let God’s glory be realized among people.
So as members of the church, let us hold to this mission and keep looking for ways to show God’s glory in our lives. Through love and service, let our lives be a testimony to God’s supreme glory.
ah: Ephesians 3:21 reminds us to desire that God receive glory in the church and in Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Take an active part in church life
Attend the church’s gatherings and activities regularly, worshiping, praying, and studying the Bible together with your brothers and sisters, and so glorify God.
Serve in the church
Volunteer for ministry in the church, whether leading worship, teaching Sunday school, welcoming guests, or other service. Give it your best so that God’s glory is displayed in the church.
Build spiritual fellowship
Build close spiritual fellowship with brothers and sisters, supporting, encouraging, and praying for one another and growing together, so that the church becomes a place that glorifies God.
Witness to Christ’s love
In daily life, treat people with love and show Christ’s love to those around you, drawing more people to know and follow God.
Persevere in prayer and thanksgiving
In good times and bad, keep praying and giving thanks, giving all the glory to God and witnessing to His work in our lives.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this passage, which reminds us that You should receive glory in the church and in Christ Jesus. Help us to take an active part in church life, to serve in the church, to build spiritual fellowship, to witness to Christ’s love, and to persevere in prayer and thanksgiving, so that our lives glorify Your name. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you live out a life in Christ that brings honor, and may the Father receive glory in your life. Amen!

t: Father and Son Glorify Each Other
v: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you;
b: These are the words Jesus spoke in His final prayer. He knew His mission was about to be completed, and He knew that His death and resurrection would bring great glory, both to Himself and to the Heavenly Father. Jesus’ whole life displayed the glory of God, and His every action and every word showed God’s love and power.

It is like an outstanding student who, on the eve of the final exam, asks his teacher for last guidance and a blessing so that he can perform at his best and bring honor to the school. Jesus does something similar here. As He is about to complete His earthly mission, He asks for the Father’s glory to come upon Him, so that at this most important moment He may display God’s perfection and glory.
