A new recruit entered a military training camp, and after months of hard training he finally became a qualified soldier. At the final ceremony the commander personally awarded him a medal of honor, because he had shown remarkable perseverance and courage in training and had won honor for the army. The recruit’s success was not only his personal achievement but the glory of the whole army. Everything Jesus did in His ministry was also to glorify the Father, so that the world could see God’s love and the power of redemption.

Each of us should also be like Jesus, striving to glorify God in every area of life. When our actions, words, and thoughts are all aligned with God’s will, our lives can become a reflection of His glory.
ah: John 17:1 reminds us that Jesus prayed to the Father, asking that the Father glorify His Son so that the Son may glorify the Father. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Live out the likeness of Christ
Learn from and imitate Christ’s humility, love, and obedience in life, and glorify God through your conduct.
Persevere in a life of prayer
Pray at set times each day, giving thanks to God and seeking His guidance, so that your prayer life shows your dependence on and reverence for Him.
Love your neighbor as yourself
Show Christ’s love in how you treat others, whether family, friends, or strangers, so that people can see Christ displayed in our lives.
Actively share the gospel
Spread the gospel with your testimony and actions, sharing what God has done in your life so that more people come to know and glorify God.
Worship and serve
Take an active part in the church’s worship and service. Singing, praying, giving, and serving are all ways to glorify God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this passage, which reminds us to glorify You and let Your glory be shown in our lives. Help us to live out the likeness of Christ, to persevere in prayer, to love our neighbors as ourselves, to share the gospel actively, and to worship and serve, so that our lives may be a witness to Your glory. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your life glorify God every day, and may you display His love and grace in everything you do. Amen!

v: I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.
b: In this passage Jesus, in His prayer, expresses to the Father how He feels about completing His mission. Jesus’ whole life and ministry were for the glory of the Father. In word, deed, and thought He was fully obedient to the Father’s will, and He brought this glory to the world.

Think of a gardener who works hard in a neglected garden, pulling weeds, fertilizing, and watering. After tireless effort the garden finally bursts into beautiful blooms, drawing everyone’s admiration and delight. The gardener’s effort has not only changed the look of the garden, but also let people see the love and devotion behind the hard work. Jesus’ work on earth was the same. By His actions and love He showed the world the Father’s glory and plan of redemption.

A doctor gave up a high-paying post in a big city and came to a remote village to give free medical care to poor villagers. Over the years he worked tirelessly and healed countless patients, and the villagers were deeply moved by his love and dedication. His actions brought not only health but also hope and the radiance of love. Jesus’ mission on earth was the same. With love and sacrifice He displayed the Father’s glory and brought us redemption and hope.

Each of us should also be like Jesus, giving our best in our own posts to complete the mission God has entrusted to us. Whatever work we do and wherever we are, we must remember that our goal is to glorify God. When we treat those around us with love and devotion, our lives can become a witness to God’s glory.
ah: John 17:4 reminds us that Jesus glorified the Father on earth and accomplished the work the Father gave Him. We too should glorify the Father on earth and complete the mission He has entrusted to us. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Be faithful to your mission
Be clear about God’s calling for each of us, whether in the workplace, the family, the church, or the community, and faithfully complete the tasks God has entrusted to us.
Daily devotions
Through daily devotions, prayer, and Bible reading, stay close to God and seek His guidance, so that we can better fulfill what He has entrusted to us.
Acts of love
Treat people with love in daily life. Whether helping those in need or showing Christ’s love in word and deed, we are glorifying God.
Sharing testimonies
Share with others what God has done in your life through your testimony and story, inspiring them to glorify God too.
Work wholeheartedly
Work with honesty, diligence, and dedication, showing the fine character of a Christian, so that your conduct becomes praise to God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this passage, which reminds us to glorify You on earth and to complete the mission You have entrusted to us. Help us to be faithful to our mission, to have daily devotions, to act in love, to share our testimonies, and to work wholeheartedly, so that our lives may be a witness to Your glory. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you glorify the Heavenly Father with love and devotion in every day of your life, and be a radiant witness to His grace. Amen!

t: The Glory Given to the Son
v: Father, I desire that they also whom you have given me be with me where I am, that they may see my glory which you have given me, for you loved me before the foundation of the world.
b: This passage comes from Jesus’ prayer after the Last Supper, a heartfelt petition to the Heavenly Father. Here Jesus expresses His desire that all who believe in Him be with Him and see the glory He has. This is not only Jesus’ love for us but also His promise to us, that we may be with Him for eternity and enjoy the Father’s love and glory.

It is like a loving father who, before his children set out on a long journey, carefully prepares a warm home for them, looking forward to their safe return and to sharing good times with them. A father’s love is everywhere, and wherever the children go they can feel the warmth of home and the father’s expectation. In the same way, Jesus has prepared an eternal dwelling for us, looking forward to our being with Him and sharing His glory and love.

A music teacher was full of love and patience for each of his students, and no matter what their talent, he always guided them wholeheartedly. Years later, some of these students became famous musicians, and some achieved remarkable things in other fields. Whenever his students succeeded, the teacher’s heart was filled with pride and joy, because their success also displayed his teaching and love. In the same way, Jesus wants us to grow in His love, to see His glory, and to glorify the Father with our lives.

In daily life, let us often remember this love and expectation of Jesus. Whatever challenges and difficulties we face, let us hold firm in faith, for we have a Savior who loves us and has prepared a good future for us. As we walk in His way, we can see His glory and glorify the Father with our lives.
ah: John 17:24 reminds us that Jesus longs for us to be with Him and to see the glory He has been given. This verse emphasizes Jesus’ love for us and our place in His glory. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Keep drawing near to God
Spend time each day in prayer and Bible reading to build a closer relationship with God and experience His love and glory.
Worship and praise
Whether at church or in private time, glorify God through praise and worship, and thank Him for His grace.
Love one another
Show Christ’s love in your interactions with others, reflecting God’s glory through care, help, and support.
Share your testimony
Share with others what God has done in your life, so that more people see God’s glory and love.
Live by faith
Whatever challenges you face, rely on God in faith and trust His plan and love, so that your life becomes a witness to His glory.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this passage, which reminds us to be with You and to see the glory You have given. Help us to keep drawing near to You, to glorify You through worship and praise, to show Your love as we love one another, to share our testimonies so that more people come to know You, and to live by faith as a witness to Your glory. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel the love and glory of Jesus every day, and witness to His grace with your life. Amen!

v: Now, Father, glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed.
b: This passage shows us Jesus’ heartfelt petition to the Father and His boundless love for each one of us. Jesus longs for us to be with Him and share His glory. This is an incomparably precious promise that lets us feel the eternal love of the Father.

It is like a warm family in which the parents always long for their children to come home and spend good times together. Parents’ love is selfless; wherever the children go, the parents’ hearts are with them, waiting for their return. In the same way, Jesus has prepared an eternal home for us and longs for us to be with Him and share His glory and love.

A beloved teacher was full of patience and love for his students. Even when they met difficulty and setbacks, he always encouraged them and helped them realize their potential. Years later these students achieved remarkable things in their own fields, and whenever they remembered their teacher’s instruction and care, their hearts were filled with gratitude and respect. The teacher’s love and devotion helped his students grow strong, and they repaid his labor with their success. In the same way, Jesus wants us to grow in His love, to see His glory, and to glorify the Father with our lives.

In daily life, let us often remember this love and expectation of Jesus. Whatever challenges and difficulties we face, let us hold firm in faith, for we have a Savior who loves us and has prepared a good future for us. As we walk in His way, we can see His glory and glorify the Father with our lives.
ah: John 17:5 reminds us that Jesus prayed to the Father, asking for the glory He shared with the Father before the world began. This verse shows us the deep relationship between Jesus and the Father, and His longing that we too would share this glory. To live out this verse in daily life, we can:
a: Pray continually
Like Jesus, we should pray often, seeking a deeper connection with the Heavenly Father and longing to share His glory spiritually.
Live out your faith
In daily life, we should witness to our faith by our conduct, so that others see Christ’s glory displayed in our lives.
Encourage one another
In the church and at home, we should encourage one another, reminding each other that we will finally share glory with God, which strengthens our confidence in facing challenges.
Serve others
Reflect Christ’s glory through love and service, taking an active part in the church, the workplace, or the community.
Spiritual growth
Set aside time each day for Bible reading, devotions, and small groups so that your spiritual life keeps growing and you experience God’s presence and glory.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this passage, which reminds us of the hope of sharing glory with You. Help us to keep praying and to seek an intimate relationship with You, so that we live out our faith and witness to Christ’s glory. May we encourage one another, serve others, and experience Your presence and glory as we grow spiritually. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you feel the love and glory of Jesus every day, and witness to His grace with your life. Amen!

v: which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had they known it, they wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.
b: This verse reminds us that human wisdom often cannot grasp God’s plan and love. In Jesus’ day, the powerful rulers of this world, because they could not recognize Jesus’ true identity and mission, actually crucified Him. Yet it was this seemingly tragic event that accomplished our salvation. Jesus’ sacrifice on the cross showed His boundless love and glory.

It is like a pearl hidden inside an unremarkable shell: only those who search patiently can discover its beauty and worth. The wisdom and glory of Jesus are a mystery hard to grasp for those whose hearts have not been opened. But for us who believe in Him, this wisdom is as precious as a pearl, worth pursuing and treasuring all our lives.

A young engineer worked hard at his company, but his superiors always rejected his innovative ideas. One day he was given a chance to help rebuild a bridge in a small village. The task seemed unimportant, but he threw himself into it and designed a bridge that was both sturdy and beautiful. Years later the bridge became the symbol of the village and attracted many visitors. The engineer was recognized and became a well-known architect. This story tells us that sometimes the world cannot see our potential and value, but if we hold on to our convictions, we will in the end be discovered and valued.

In the same way, when we face being misunderstood or overlooked, let us remember Jesus’ sacrifice and glory on the cross and keep walking in His way. In God’s timing our faith and actions will reveal His glory, and our lives will shine with a heavenly light.
ah: Dear family, peace to you. Let us follow together today’s Soul Snack action guide. 1 Corinthians 2:8 reminds us that even among those in power, true wisdom and the glory of Jesus Christ are often not recognized. If they had truly understood who Jesus is, they would not have crucified Him. From this verse we can learn to seek and display God’s wisdom and glory in daily life with a humble heart:
a: Humbly learn God’s wisdom

Spend time every day studying the Bible, especially Jesus’ teachings in the Gospels, and let God’s Word be the guide for our decisions, words, and actions. 2. Discern and reject worldly wisdom: When you face pressure from society or culture, use the truth of Scripture to test whether those ideas agree with God’s will, and avoid blindly following trends that go against it.
Show Christ’s love in your relationships
Christ’s glory is found not only in His divinity but also in His unconditional love for us. In daily life, whether at work, at home, or among friends, treat others with love and compassion.
Witness to Jesus’ lordship and glory in hardship
When you face trials and challenges, remember that Jesus has overcome the world. Keep your faith in hardship, and show others Jesus’ lordship and glory through your attitude and actions.
Take an active part in church and community service
In the church and the community, look for opportunities to serve, and through practical action show Jesus’ love and glory and help those in need.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your boundless wisdom and glory to us through Your Son Jesus Christ. Give us humble hearts to learn and follow Your wisdom and not to follow the trends of this world. Help us in daily life to love others as ourselves and to show Your glory in every circumstance. May our lives be a witness that glorifies You and draws more people to know You. We pray in the name of the victorious Lord Jesus, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. In daily life, whatever challenges you meet, may you hold on to your faith and show the wisdom and glory God has given you. Amen!

v: His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, who, when he had by himself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high,
b: This verse shows us the supreme glory and divinity of Jesus Christ. He is the radiance of God’s glory and the true image of God’s being. He upholds all things by His power, and He paid the price for our sins, and now sits at the right hand of the Most High.

Like a lighthouse that guides lost ships home across a dark sea, Jesus is the lighthouse of our lives, lighting our way forward and leading us back into God’s arms. The light of this lighthouse never goes out, and it symbolizes Jesus’ eternal love and unchanging guidance.

A new army recruit kept failing in training at first and felt hopeless about his future. But his instructor did not give up on him. Instead he coached him with care, giving encouragement and support. The instructor’s patience and wisdom gradually changed the recruit, and he eventually became an outstanding soldier. He later recalled, “My instructor’s guidance and encouragement gave me confidence and changed my life.” Jesus’ love and guidance for us is like this instructor. He lights up our lives with His radiance and brings us hope and the power to change.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us look to Jesus every day and draw strength and wisdom from Him. Whatever challenges we face, let us remember that Jesus’ radiance always shines on us. He upholds all things by His power, and He has washed away our sins so that we can draw near to God.
ah: Hebrews 1:3 tells us that Jesus Christ is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact image of His being. He upholds all things by His word, He has made purification for our sins, and He now sits at the right hand of the Majesty on high. To live out this truth in our lives, we can take these concrete actions:
a: Daily meditation and prayer
Take time to reflect on the fact that Jesus is the radiance of God’s glory. In prayer, thank Him for cleansing our sins and ask Him to help us live out His likeness.
Study and share God’s Word
Commit to reading God’s Word every day, and look for opportunities to share with others how God has shown His glory through Jesus in your life.
Look to Jesus in hardship
When you face challenges and trials, remember that Jesus is the One who upholds all things. Ask Him for strength and wisdom to overcome these difficulties in His way.
Practice forgiveness and kindness
Just as Jesus has cleansed our sins, we should show forgiveness and kindness to those around us. Practice forgiveness in your relationships and witness to His grace.
Live a godly life
Jesus sitting at the right hand of the Majesty on high is our ultimate example and hope. Let us strive to show heavenly values and conduct in our lives, so that they reflect the kingdom of God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for letting us see Your glory through Your Son Jesus Christ. Help us to live in Your radiance every day, not only looking to Jesus but also displaying Your glory before others. When we face challenges in life, remind us that You are the God who upholds all things. Give us strength to forgive others, and to glorify You with holy and godly lives. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience Jesus’ radiance in your life, feel His love and power, and bring this light to those around you. Amen!

v: seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
b: This verse reminds us that God’s light shines in our hearts so that we can see God’s glory displayed in the face of Jesus Christ. God’s light shines out of darkness, lighting up not only our outward circumstances but also the depths of our hearts.

It is like a pitch-dark night when a bright ray of light suddenly cuts through the darkness, bringing hope and direction. Jesus Christ is such a light. His light not only guides us forward but lets us feel God’s glory and love.

Here is a moving story. A young girl named Lisa lost her sight in early childhood and lived in darkness. Yet her heart did not grow dim. Led by her mother, Lisa came to know Jesus Christ and felt His light. She said, “Although I cannot see the brightness of this world, Jesus’ love fills my heart with light.” Later Lisa became a motivational speaker and inspired countless people with her experience.

Dear brothers and sisters, whatever difficulty or darkness we face in life, remember that God’s light has already shone in our hearts. This light is God’s glory, displayed in the face of Jesus Christ. Let us open the door of our hearts and let this light into our lives, to drive away all darkness and bring hope and strength.
ah: 2 Corinthians 4:6 emphasizes that the light of God’s glory shines in our hearts so that we know Jesus Christ. This passage guides us in how to live out this truth in daily life:
a: Pursue spiritual awakening
Spend time each day in prayer and Bible reading seeking God’s face, and let God’s Word be the guide and light of our lives.
Reflect on your life
Examine your way of life and think about which areas need God’s light to illuminate and change them.
Practice transparency and honesty
Show honesty and transparency in your relationships. Just as God’s light shines in darkness, we should be lights of honesty.
Serve and witness
By serving the community and helping others, let people see God’s light through our actions.
Keep improving yourself
Keep learning and growing, whether spiritually, intellectually, or in skills, so that God’s light shines more brightly through us.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the power by which You commanded light to shine out of darkness. Light up our hearts so that in daily life we reflect the light of Your glory. Help us to witness to Your love and glory as we pursue spiritual awakening, practice transparency and honesty, serve and witness, and keep improving ourselves. Make us a reflection of Your glory, shining for Your kingdom not only in the church but in society. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God’s light shine in your heart, so that every day you feel His love and glory. Amen!

v: For he received from God the Father honor and glory when the voice came to him from the Majestic Glory, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
b: This verse describes the moment on the Mount of Transfiguration when Jesus Christ received glory from God the Father, a moving moment when the Heavenly Father publicly affirmed His only Son. This scene is not only an affirmation of Jesus but a reminder to all believers: the Christ we believe in has been personally attested by the Heavenly Father.

In a family, when a father praises his child in front of everyone, how powerful the feeling of honor and approval is! It is not only an affirmation of the child but a public endorsement of what the child has done. In the same way, in our spiritual lives, when we live in Christ, we are also seeking the Heavenly Father’s approval and glory.

A young man had always worked hard in his studies and career, hoping to win his parents’ approval and encouragement. When he finally received praise at an important meeting, his father said to him publicly, “Son, I am proud of you, and I love you.” Those simple words gave him tremendous encouragement and strength.

In our daily lives, whatever our profession or stage of life, when we strive to live in the likeness of Christ, showing love, humility, and a servant heart, we too are seeking glory from our Heavenly Father, just as He publicly glorified His Son.
ah: 2 Peter 1:17 describes the moment Jesus received honor and glory from God the Father, reminding us of God’s love for Jesus and His delight in Him. This verse encourages us to reflect God’s love for us in our words and deeds in daily life, and to seek His approval. Here are some concrete steps:
a: An intimate prayer life
Set a regular time for prayer each day, focusing on thanking God for His love and seeking His guidance, so that God’s voice becomes the compass of our lives.
Deeper Bible study
Study the Bible regularly, especially the parts about Jesus’ life and ministry, and learn from them how to be children that please God.
Reflect God’s love
In your interactions with family, friends, and coworkers, show Jesus’ love and compassion, especially to those who need comfort and help.
Find your role in church service
According to your gifts and interests, take an active part in the church’s ministries. This is not only a response to God’s call but also a way to bring glory to God.
Keep faith in challenges
When you face trials and difficulties in life, hold on to your faith and overcome with patience and perseverance, showing what makes the people of God different.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, You are the God of glory. The delight You expressed in Your beloved Son Jesus is also Your heart toward each of Your children. Give us strength and wisdom so that our lives may reflect Your glory, and that our words and actions may be a witness to Your love. Help us seek Your approval in daily life and grow in Your love. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your conduct in Christ win the Father’s delight and glory, just as He did with Jesus. Amen!

t: Through the Glory of the Father
v: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
b: This verse reminds us that through baptism we are buried with Christ and raised with Him. Our lives thus become entirely new, and our every action should show this new life.

Like a seed buried in the soil that changes quietly and finally breaks through the ground to become a flourishing plant, our life of faith also needs to go through such renewal and change. This renewal does not come from ourselves, but through the glory of the Father, just as Christ was raised from the dead.

A young man had lived a wild and reckless life, and his relationships with his family and friends were broken. One day he decided to change, received Jesus Christ, and was born again through baptism. From then on his every action showed a new life. He began to care about others, joined community service, and mended his relationships with family and friends. His transformation was like a seed breaking through the ground, bringing new life and hope.

Each of us should remember that baptism is the starting point of our new life. Through the glory of the Father, we too can be born again out of our past and live a new life full of hope and love. We should live out this newness in daily life, letting our words and conduct display Christ’s love and glory.
ah: Romans 6:4 teaches us that through baptism we die, are buried, and are raised with Christ, showing the character of new life. This process reflects the wonderful truth that Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father. Here are some practical steps to help us live out this truth in daily life:
a: Daily renewal

When you get up in the morning, spend a few minutes in prayer, offering the new day to God and reminding yourself that, because of Christ’s resurrection, we have been freed from the bondage of the old life.
Victory over temptation and sin
When you face temptation or challenge, recall the new life and power that Christ’s resurrection has given us, and overcome through that power.
Live out resurrection hope
In your conversations and conduct at work, at home, and among friends, show the hope and joy of Christ’s resurrection.
Serve and witness
Through service in the church and community, bear witness to the transforming power of the resurrection life and help others experience that change too.
Celebrate and give thanks
Regularly share in your group or church the changes you have experienced in Christ through your faith, to celebrate and thank God for His grace.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us the hope and power of new life through the death and resurrection of Your Son Jesus Christ. Help us to live out this new life every day, and in whatever situation to overcome and conquer by the power of the resurrection. May our lives be a witness to Your glory, so that more people come to know Your glory and power through our testimony. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May every step of your life show this new life, live out the likeness of Christ, and display the glory of the Heavenly Father. Amen!

v: When he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.
b: “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.”

This passage reminds us that Jesus Christ, in His life, death, and resurrection, displayed the glory of God. Every step of His path showed God’s power and love, and through His sacrifice God was glorified in the Son of Man.

Like a diamond that shows its brilliance only through cutting and polishing, Jesus showed God’s glory in His suffering. That brilliance lies not only in His divinity but is revealed in His obedience and sacrifice, reaching its peak at last on the cross.

A brave firefighter, in a raging fire, disregarded his own safety, rushed into a smoke-filled building, and rescued many people trapped in the flames. His courage and selfless act deeply moved people, and everyone saw the glory and radiance in his heart. In the same way, the sacrifice and love of Jesus Christ let us see the glory of God.

Jesus’ glory lies in all that He did for us. With His life He proved God’s love for us. We should follow His example, so that our lives too can display God’s glory. When we meet challenges and difficulties in life, let us remember Jesus’ example and be willing to give of ourselves for others, so that God’s love is displayed through our actions.
ah: In John 13:31, Jesus declares that the Son of Man is glorified in carrying out God’s will, and that through the Son of Man’s obedience God is glorified too. This reveals the deep connection between obedience and glory. Here are some concrete guidelines to help us live out this truth in daily life:
a: Seek glory through obedience
In daily decisions and conduct, choose to obey God’s will rather than human opinion or personal desire, recognizing that obedience is the road to spiritual glory.
See difficulties as opportunities for glory
When you face challenges and difficulties in life, see them as opportunities to show loyalty and faith toward God, as Jesus showed in His experience on the cross.
Witness in the community and the workplace
By keeping an attitude of integrity and kindness in hard situations, let our lives be a witness to God’s glory and influence others to pursue such a life.
Seek glory in church service
Take an active part in the church’s service and activities, using our gifts and abilities to glorify God and encouraging others to join in serving.
Practice glory in family relationships
Practice Jesus’ teaching in the family, building harmony through love, tolerance, and forgiveness, so that our homes become a witness to God’s glory.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for showing us true glory through Your Son Jesus Christ. Help us to learn obedience in every area of life, whether in hardship, in community service, or in the family and the workplace. May our lives be a witness to Your glory, so that more people come to know Your love and grace. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your life be filled with the glory of Jesus, and may the glory God has in the Son of Man also be seen in your life. Amen!

t: God Glorifies the Son of Man
v: If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and he will glorify him immediately.
b: This passage reminds us that God displayed His own glory in the life and ministry of Jesus Christ. Every action and every word of Jesus reflected God’s greatness and love, and because of Jesus’ obedience and sacrifice, God received glory.

It is like a skilled musician playing a moving piece on stage, every note full of life and passion, enthralling the audience. In the same way, Jesus’ whole life is like such a piece, every step showing God’s love and glory and drawing us close to Him.

A young teacher named John taught at a primary school in a poor area. He not only taught conscientiously but often used his spare time to tutor students from struggling families. Once a student faced the crisis of dropping out because of family hardship. Teacher John not only solved the tuition problem for this student but tutored him personally, and in the end the student graduated with excellent grades and won a university scholarship. The teacher’s love and dedication is like the glory God displays in us through Jesus, letting us see God’s goodness and lovingkindness.

In life we too can follow Jesus, letting God’s glory be displayed through our conduct. When we work diligently, treat others with love and patience, and rely on God’s strength in challenges, our lives become vessels that bear witness to God’s glory.
ah: John 13:32 reminds us that God displayed His glory in Jesus Christ, and that this display of glory was swift and striking. This verse teaches us to see how God carries out His purpose through His Son and glorifies Himself in the process. Here are concrete ways to apply this truth in our daily lives:
a: Respond quickly to God’s call
When we sense God’s leading, or God speaking to us through the Holy Spirit, we should respond quickly and obediently. This shows that we trust and honor God’s authority.
Seek God’s glory in service
Whether in the church or in community service, our motive should be to glorify God rather than to seek personal recognition or glory.
Show faith in difficult times
Even when we face challenges and trials in life, keep a firm faith and show our reliance on the power of God’s glory.
Glorify God through personal testimony
In our testimonies, honestly share how God has worked in our lives, including our changes and growth, so that others can see God’s work.
Cultivate expectation of God’s glory
In prayer and devotions, focus on expecting God to display even greater glory in the future, which will strengthen our faith in and reverence for God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, You are the source of glory and power. Thank You for displaying Your glory through Your Son Jesus Christ. Help us to respond to Your call quickly and obediently in daily life, and whether through service, testimony, or holding on to faith in trials, to let our lives glorify You. Give us sensitive hearts to seek Your glory in all things, and to expect even greater glory to be displayed in our lives and service. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God’s glory be shown everywhere in your life, and may your life be a witness that glorifies God. Amen!

v: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
b: These words of Jesus remind us that the disciples who follow Him will share His glory and authority in the coming kingdom of heaven. This is a promise to all who faithfully follow Christ: our effort and faith in this life will be rewarded and recognized in the future.

It is like a gardener who works hard, caring for each plant with great attention. Sowing and tending take a great deal of time and energy, but when harvest season finally comes, the abundant fruit brings him immense satisfaction and joy. In the same way, as we follow Christ we may face challenges and difficulties, but all that we give is worthwhile, because in the eternal kingdom we will share glory with Christ.

A faithful Christian named Mark held to his faith in the Lord no matter how great the difficulties and challenges he met. He often took part in the various ministries of the church and cared for and helped people in need, and became an example to everyone. Years later Mark unfortunately fell seriously ill, but he still faced each day with firm faith and a joyful heart. He told those around him that he was convinced he would sit with the Lord on a throne of glory in the kingdom of heaven, and this gave him immense comfort and strength.

Jesus’ words inspire us to follow Him faithfully in this life, and not to give up whatever challenges we meet. Let us firmly believe that in the kingdom of heaven to come, we will share glory and joy with the Lord.
ah: Matthew 19:28 reminds us of the promise Jesus made to those who follow Him: that in the future they will share His glory and take part in important responsibilities in God’s kingdom. This verse encourages us to keep faithful on the road of following Jesus and to look forward to the glory to come. Here are some practical ways to apply this verse in daily life:
a: Deepen your spiritual commitment
Through prayer and Bible study each day, grow in your knowledge and following of Jesus, and strengthen your loyalty to Him.
Live a life of service
Look for opportunities to serve in the church and the community, imitating Jesus’ spirit of service, and showing your faith through practical action.
Cultivate patience and perseverance
When you face trials and challenges, be patient, remember Jesus’ promise, and focus on the glory that is finally to come.
Take an active part in the church
Take part in the church’s decision-making and activities, leading by example and promoting the unity and growth of the church.
Teach and nurture others
Just as we will one day judge from thrones, begin now to guide and help others grow spiritually, and become a mentor in the faith.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us, through Your Son Jesus Christ, the promise of glory and honor that we will finally share. Give us faithfulness and courage to keep following Jesus in good times and bad, to live a life of service, and by Your grace to help others grow. As we look forward to the day we sit on thrones of glory, let our lives be a witness to Your love and righteousness. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you stand firm in faith on the road of following Christ, serve faithfully, and in the future share glory with the Lord in the kingdom of heaven. Amen!

t: The Glory of the Son of Man
v: “But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
b: This passage paints a picture of a future full of hope and glory: when Jesus Christ comes again, He will be in glory with the angels and will sit on His throne of glory to judge. For all of us who believe, this is not only a warning but a comfort, because we know that the Savior we hope for will surely come again and bring eternal justice and peace.

It is like a farmer working hard in the field. Though he faces the burning sun and the wind and rain every day, in his heart he always holds the hope of harvest. Every plowing and every sowing is so that one day he may see a full harvest. In the same way, everything we do in this world, whether good deeds or service for the Lord, is preparation for the glory to come.

A missionary named John spent decades proclaiming the gospel in remote places, living simply and helping the local people. Yet facing hard conditions and voices that did not understand, he held on to his faith in God and his zeal for his mission. When people asked why he was so persistent, he would always smile and say, “I believe that when the Lord comes again, I will be with Him and see His glory, and all this effort will have been worth it.”

Jesus’ return is not only the vindication of our faith but also the greatest encouragement to each of us who faithfully follow Him. Whatever challenges and difficulties we face, as long as we stand firm in faith and hold on to hope, the Lord’s glory will become our strength and joy.
ah: Today’s verse reminds us that when Jesus Christ comes again, He will come in supreme glory and sit on His throne of glory for judgment. This passage encourages us to live in a way that fits the kingdom of God, preparing to welcome Jesus’ return. Here are some suggestions for putting this truth into practice in daily life:
a: Live out justice and compassion
Seek fairness and justice in daily life, and treat everyone with Christ’s love and fairness.
Serve others
Find opportunities to help people in need, whether through the church’s service projects or volunteer activities in the community.
Cultivate spiritual alertness
Through prayer, Bible study, and fellowship, keep our hearts alert and ready for the Lord’s return at any time.
Spread the gospel
Actively share the gospel with unbelievers, so that more people come to know Jesus and look forward to His return.
Examine your life
Regularly check whether your life reflects Jesus’ teachings and whether you are faithful to His will in every way.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, help us to live out Your will faithfully as we wait for Your beloved Son, our Savior Jesus Christ, to come again. Make us people of justice and compassion, active in serving others, and prepared in Your kingdom for the throne of glory. Give us courage and wisdom to shine like lights in the world and lead others to know You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be motivated every day by the glory of the Lord’s return, serve faithfully, and stand firm in faith until that day of glory comes. Amen!

v: Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
b: This passage tells us that Christ Jesus, through His suffering, finally entered into glory. This was not only His appointed destiny but also His promise to each of us. There is an inseparable relationship between Jesus’ suffering and glory, because His suffering opened for us the door to glory.

It is like a seed buried in dark soil, going through cold and damp, and finally breaking through to become a sturdy tree. The life of this seed tells us that only through suffering and challenge can a good harvest come. In the same way, Christ’s suffering has prepared a glorious future for us, reminding us to hold on to our faith in hardship, because glory lies ahead.

A believer named Anna had suffered from a serious illness since childhood, and physical pain accompanied her growing up. Yet Anna never gave up her faith in God. She prayed every day, seeking God’s will, and even in pain she still smiled and encouraged those around her. One day in prayer she felt God’s presence, and her heart was filled with peace and strength. She said, “My suffering is deep, but I know that this suffering is only temporary, because God’s glory is waiting for me.”
Anna’s story shows us that whatever challenges and difficulties we face in life, we must remember Christ’s suffering and glory. His suffering was for our salvation, and His glory is our final hope.

When we face hardship in life, let us keep Christ’s example in mind, hold firm in faith, and walk toward the road of glory. For everyone who follows Christ will in the end enter that kingdom of glory with Him.
ah: Today’s verse reminds us that Christ entered His glory through suffering. This passage encourages us to realize that in suffering there is also God’s purpose and plan. Here are some suggestions for putting this truth into practice in daily life:
a: Accept trials
When you face difficulties and challenges in life, accept them with a positive attitude, knowing that these experiences can train our faith and bring us closer to God.
Seek God’s will
In adversity, seek God’s will through prayer and Bible study, looking for what God teaches and how He guides us in each difficulty.
Share your testimony
Share with others how you have experienced God’s presence and leading in suffering. This not only encourages others but also strengthens your own faith.
Keep a thankful heart
Even in hard times, remember to thank God for each day and each opportunity to learn.
Help others carry their burdens
When you see people around you going through difficulty, reach out to help and share their burdens together. This is a concrete act of Christian love.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for showing us, through the suffering and glory of Your Son Jesus Christ, the victory and meaning in suffering. Give us a faith that stands firm in hardship, so that we find meaning in our own suffering and can also help others through their difficult times. Help us to seek Your glory in everything, and after suffering to experience Your grace and glory. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you see hope in Christ’s suffering and find strength in His glory, hold on to your faith, and walk toward a bright future. Amen!

v: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will give to everyone according to his deeds.
b: This verse reminds us that Jesus Christ will come in the glory of His Father, and that He will repay us according to our deeds. This is not only a warning but the hope of our faith. When Jesus comes again, He will bring justice and glory, and a reward for those who have faithfully served Him on earth.

It is like a farmer who works the land diligently and waits patiently for harvest day. Though there are storms, scorching heat, and cold along the way, the farmer persists, because he knows that as long as he does not give up, harvest time will come. In the same way, on our journey of faith we will meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties, but as long as we hold on to our faith, Jesus will surely respond to our faithfulness with His glory.

A sister named Mary worked at a charity. Every day she tirelessly helped those in need, whether homeless people or families needing food, and Mary always gave her best. One cold winter day, as she delivered food to an elderly man, he held her hand and said gratefully, “You are an angel sent from God.” Mary answered with a smile, “All this is God’s love flowing among us. I am only His instrument.”

Mary’s story tells us that everyone who serves faithfully, in great things or small, is preparing for Jesus’ return. When He comes with the angels, He will repay us according to our deeds. This is our encouragement and our hope.
Dear brothers and sisters, let us keep doing good in daily life, and whatever challenges and difficulties we face, remember Jesus’ promise. For He will come in glory and bring us an eternal reward.
ah: Today’s verse reminds us that Jesus Christ will come with the angels in the glory of His Father and will repay each person according to his deeds. This verse stresses responsibility and being ready for the judgment to come. Here are some ways to put this teaching into practice:
a: Reflect on daily conduct
Each evening take time to reflect on your conduct and consider whether it reflects Christian character and values.
Study and apply the Bible
Study the Bible regularly, seek to understand what God requires in justice and love, and strive to practice these teachings in daily life.
Take an active part in service
Join in the church’s and the community’s service activities, showing Christ’s love and glory through practical action.
The mission of spreading the gospel
Take opportunities to proclaim the gospel to others, so that more people can come to know Jesus Christ and prepare for His return.
Hold on to faith and patience
In the face of the world’s challenges and temptations, keep firm faith and patience, remembering that our final hope is to be with the Lord.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the promise of our future through Your Son Jesus Christ. Help us to live a life that reflects Your glory, so that our words and actions please You. While we wait for Your kingdom to come, give us wisdom and strength to be Your witnesses in the world, with Your glory as our highest goal. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you witness to Christ’s love in your actions every day, and receive His reward when He comes again. Amen!

v: who will change the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working by which he is able even to subject all things to himself.
b: This verse gives us great hope and comfort. Our bodies now are limited and go through pain, sickness, and aging, but God promises that by His great power He will change these lowly bodies of ours to be like His glorious body. What a promise and what glory!

It is like a caterpillar transforming into a butterfly. In the chrysalis the caterpillar goes through many changes, and finally breaks out of the cocoon as a beautiful butterfly. In the same way, on the journey of this life we go through all kinds of challenges and tests, but they are God’s carving and shaping in our lives. When at last we meet the Lord, like the butterfly we will shed the old body and put on a new body of glory.

A brother named Wayne lost the ability to move in a serious car accident. The doctors told him he would never walk again. Wayne went through great pain and discouragement, but he did not give up his faith. He prayed every day in his hospital bed and drew strength from God’s Word. He believed that although his body was limited, his soul had hope in God’s hands. One day he said to a friend who visited him, “I know that one day God will give me a glorious body, and then I will no longer be bound by these limits.”
Wayne’s faith and perseverance remind us that whatever our circumstances now, we must look to God’s promise. In His time, by His great power, God will change us to be like His glorious body.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us face challenges with hope and faith in each day of life. Remember that God’s power is able to do all things, and His promise will surely be fulfilled. Let this encourage us to keep walking the road of faith until that day of glory comes.
ah: Today’s verse reminds us that the Lord Jesus Christ has the authority and power to change our limited and lowly bodies in the future to be like His glorious body. This is not only a promise for the future but also a guide for living out our faith now. Here are some ways to put this teaching into practice:
a: Offer your body
Offer your body to God as a holy vessel, avoid unhealthy or harmful behavior, and actively keep your body healthy.
Renew your mind
Through prayer, meditation, and Bible study, let your mind be renewed day by day, so that our thoughts and feelings reflect Christ’s glory.
Serve and witness
Take an active part in service in the church and community, witnessing to Christ’s glory by action, so that others see Christ’s love and power through our lives.
Seek holiness
Pursue holiness in speech, conduct, and daily decisions, and avoid everything that separates people from God.
Waiting and hope
Wait for the Lord’s return with a positive attitude, encouraging yourself and those around you with hope, and believing that God will fulfill His promise.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us the promise of glory through Your great power. Help us to regard our bodies as Your temple and to show Your glory in daily life. May we be renewed in mind, clean in conduct, and zealous in service, keep seeking a relationship with You, and look forward to the fulfillment of Your promise. Give us strength and wisdom to live out Your glory while we wait for it to appear. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength and hope in God’s promises, and witness to His great power in every day of your life. Amen!

v: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you. On their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.
b: This verse reminds us that when we are insulted or face hardship because of our faith in Christ, we are blessed. This is not because of the hardship itself, but because the Spirit of God’s glory is with us and gives us strength and comfort.

It is like a tree in a storm: the deeper its roots, the better it can withstand wind and rain. Our faith is the same. In hardship, the deeper our roots go in Christ, the more unshakable we become. God’s Spirit works within us, giving us strength and wisdom so that we can face challenges and witness to His glory.

A sister named Yalan was mocked and shunned at her workplace because she held to her faith. Yet she did not shrink back. Instead, every morning she prayed, asking God for wisdom and courage. In the face of difficulty she still kept doing what was upright and kind, and treated everyone with love. Her attitude and conduct finally moved her coworkers, and some began to ask her about her faith and gradually accepted the gospel.

This story tells us that when we meet hardship because of Christ’s name, we should stand firm in faith, because God’s Spirit is with us and His glory is displayed in our lives. Hardship is not only a test but also an opportunity to witness to God’s glory.

Dear family, when we face difficulty, let us remember that God’s Spirit is with us and gives us strength and courage. With faith and love let us meet the challenges of life, witness to God’s glory, and bring hope and light to others.
ah: Today’s verse reminds us that when we are persecuted or insulted for our faith in Christ, we are actually blessed, because it means the Spirit of God’s glory is with us. Here are some ways to put this teaching into practice:
a: Keep a positive attitude
When you face persecution or misunderstanding, keep a positive and forgiving attitude, believing that this is an opportunity from God for us to show true Christian character.
Live out your witness
Even in adversity, keep showing Christ’s love and grace, so that people see the difference Christ makes through our conduct.
Deepen your devotional life
Through prayer, meditation, and Bible study, deepen your knowledge of God so that you can hold your faith in persecution.
Build a support network
Stay closely connected with brothers and sisters in the church community and faith groups, supporting and encouraging one another and facing persecution together.
Serve and give
Look for opportunities to serve in the community, and do not stop doing good even when misunderstood or opposed, as a response to God’s love.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, give us strength and courage, and when we are insulted for Your name, let us remember this is a sign of blessing, because Your Spirit is with us. Help us in adversity still to respond with Christ’s love, and to witness to Your glory through our lives. May our conduct and attitude encourage others to know You, and make us ever firmer on the road of faith. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s presence in difficulty and become a witness to His glory. Amen!

v: that he might present the assembly to himself gloriously, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without defect.
b: This verse tells us that God wants us to be a glorious church, holy and without blemish. This is not just a lofty ideal but a concrete, achievable goal. How do we reach it? First, we must understand that holiness is not only outward behavior but an inner condition of the heart, our complete devotion to and love for God.

It is like a gardener carefully tending his garden, removing weeds and pruning branches so that every flower can bloom in its most beautiful form. In the same way, God prunes us in our lives, removing what does not belong to Him so that we may become vessels that please Him.

A sister named Lisa used to be impatient and quick-tempered, but after coming to faith she resolved to change and become more like Christ. Whenever she felt angry or discouraged, she would pray to God at once, asking Him for calm and wisdom. After a long time of effort and prayer, Lisa became more and more gentle and peaceful, and her life gradually gave off the fragrance of Christ.
Lisa’s story tells us that as long as we are willing to commit ourselves to God and let Him work in our lives, we can become that glorious church, without spot or wrinkle, holy and without blemish.
Dear family, let us strive together to pursue holiness and be a church that pleases God. Let us pray to God every day, asking Him to prune our lives so that we can live out His glory.
ah: Today’s verse inspires us: the church is the bride of Christ and should be glorious, without spot, wrinkle, or any blemish. Here are concrete ways to put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: Pursue holiness
On a personal level, devote yourself to spiritual growth, stay away from sin, and pursue a holy life. This includes repenting often and practicing the principles of Scripture in daily life.
Cultivate love and fellowship
In the church community, actively build and maintain love and care for one another. This includes supporting one another, being patient and forgiving, with Christ’s love at the center.
Take part in service

Take an active part in the various ministries of the church, so that the church becomes a community that displays God’s glory to the world. Each member’s service is not only fulfilling a duty but also an expression of love for God and commitment to the church.
Keep learning and growing
Through Bible study, Bible study groups, and Bible classes, keep growing in understanding and practicing God’s Word. Let the teaching of Scripture sink deep into our thoughts and conduct.
Witness to Christ
Live out your faith in the community and the workplace, witnessing to Christ’s transforming power by action and drawing more people to know the Lord.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us, through Your Son Jesus Christ, the opportunity to become a glorious church. Help us to live in Your holiness every day, so that our words and conduct glorify You. Guide us to be witnesses of love and service, so that our church is without spot or wrinkle, holy and without blemish. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s presence and blessing on the road of pursuing holiness, and become a witness to His glory. Amen!

v: according to the Good News of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
b: This verse reminds us that the gospel is not only good news but a sacred trust. God has entrusted this glorious gospel to us, expecting us to be its messengers. The gospel is God’s power, able to change lives and bring hope and salvation.

It is like a tree that buds in spring and, nourished by sunshine and rain, finally bears abundant fruit. The power of the gospel is the same. When we receive it and pass it on, it takes root in people’s hearts and brings changed lives and abundant fruit.

A sister named Liz lived in a small town. Her family was harmonious and her job was steady, but she always felt something was missing from her life. Then one day she met an evangelist on the street, who told her that Jesus loved her and could fill the emptiness in her heart. At first Liz went to church activities just to give it a try. But as time went by, she was drawn by Jesus’ love and decided to give her life to the Lord. Liz’s life was made new. She no longer felt empty but was filled with joy and hope. Now she is a zealous evangelist, bringing this glorious gospel to those around her.
Liz’s story tells us that the gospel has boundless power to change hearts and bring new life. Each of us can be like Liz, a witness to God’s gospel, bringing this love and hope to more people.

Dear family, let us commit ourselves together to spreading this glorious gospel. Whether in our families, our workplaces, or our communities, we can all be messengers of the gospel. May God give us courage and wisdom to complete this mission faithfully and become vessels of His glory.
ah: Today’s verse encourages us to spread the glorious gospel widely, the precious mission God has entrusted to us. Here are ways we can put this verse into practice in daily life:
a: Learn and prepare
Keep learning God’s Word so that you are always ready to explain and share the reason for the gospel. This may include taking gospel training courses and reading theology books or the Bible.
Live out your witness
Show the standard of Christian living through your daily conduct, so that people see Christ’s love and change through our words and actions.
Share actively

Use every opportunity, whether at work, at home, or in social settings, to share the gospel and your personal faith experience. This can be through conversation, sharing testimonies, or even social media.
Serve the community
Serve in the community, for example by joining charity activities or supporting the vulnerable, showing Christ’s love through action. This is also an effective gospel witness.
Support through prayer
Pray for the spread of the gospel and for the softening of the hearts of those who hear it, and also for coworkers serving in gospel work, asking God to give them wisdom and strength.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for entrusting the glorious gospel to us. Help us to learn actively and share Your truth boldly in daily life. May our words and conduct be a witness to Your love and glory and draw more people to know You. Use us so that more people experience the salvation and hope this glorious gospel brings. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s abundant grace and presence on the road of spreading the gospel, and be a blessing in many people’s lives. Amen!

v: Yours, LORD, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, LORD, and you are exalted as head above all.
b: This verse reminds us that God is supreme, and that all glory, power, and majesty are His. Whatever challenges and difficulties we meet on earth, let us remember that the God we believe in is the almighty ruler, and everything is in His hands.

It is like a great conductor: with a gentle wave of the baton the whole orchestra moves along, playing a harmonious and pleasing piece. God is such a perfect conductor. He governs the whole universe, and everything is within His plan and purpose.

Here is a story from a small town. A young farmer, after several years of drought in a row, had almost no harvest from his fields, and his life fell into hardship. His heart was full of confusion and despair. One day he heard this verse at church, and the pastor told him that God is almighty and that all glory and power are His. The young farmer began to put his trust in God, praying every day and believing that God would provide for his needs in His own time. Before long rain fell from heaven, and his fields brought in a rich harvest. This taught him God’s power and faithfulness and made him firmer in his faith.

This story shows us that when we entrust our difficulties to God, He will accomplish everything in His own way. Whatever we face, as long as we believe in God’s power and glory, He will surely lead us through every hardship.

Dear family, let us always remember God’s almighty power and glory in life. Whatever challenges we face, let us hold firm in faith and rely on His strength. Believe that God’s plan is far beyond our imagination, and that He will guide our every step with His glory.
ah: Today’s verse shows us that all glory belongs to God, who is the ruler of the whole universe. Here are concrete ways to put this verse into practice in daily life:
a: Praise and worship
In daily prayer and worship, devote yourself to praising God’s greatness and glory. Whether in private devotions or public worship, let praise be the focus.
Acknowledge God’s sovereignty
When you face decisions or difficulties, actively seek God’s will and acknowledge His sovereignty in our lives. This shows in seeking God’s guidance in daily choices and in planning for the future.
A life of thanksgiving
Give thanks often for all the grace and blessings God gives, big or small. This includes not only material blessings but every opportunity for growth and learning in life.
Proclaim God’s power
By sharing your personal testimony or what God has done in your life, let others see God’s glory. This can be done in group sharing, church testimony, or outreach.
Serve and give

Devote your time, talents, or resources to serving others and the church, and so show God’s glory. In service, show God’s love and power, whether in community service, church ministry, or caring for your family.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, all greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty belong to You. Help us in daily life to display Your glory through praise, service, thanksgiving, and testimony. May our lives be a platform that shows Your supreme sovereignty to the world. We long to glorify You in all things, and we thank You that You are the Most High God in our lives. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength and peace in God’s glory and experience His wonderful works. Amen!

v: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
b: This verse is the ending of the Lord’s Prayer, reminding us that all glory, power, and kingdom belong to God forever. The teaching here is not only a request for God’s protection but an acknowledgment of God’s almighty power and sovereignty.

It is like a great king whose kingdom is boundless and whose subjects all live under his protection and guidance. God is such a supreme King. He rules over all, protects us, and leads us through the various challenges of life.

A young student faced an important exam in life. The pressure was enormous, and he often felt anxious and uneasy. His parents encouraged him to rely on his faith and hand his difficulties to God in prayer every day. He began to quote this verse in his prayers, asking for God’s protection and guidance. As a result, he not only did excellently in the exam but also learned to rely on God’s strength under pressure and found peace within.

This story tells us that whatever temptations and challenges we face, as long as we entrust everything to God, He will surely lead us, and His kingdom, power, and glory belong to Him forever. In our lives we will inevitably meet all kinds of difficulties and temptations, but by God’s strength we can receive protection and guidance, because He is our King forever.

Dear family, let us always remember the truth of this verse in life, giving all glory and thanks to God, and relying on His protection and guidance in every challenge. Whatever temptation we face, remember that God’s kingdom, power, and glory belong to Him forever.
ah: Today’s verse reminds us that all kingdom, power, and glory belong to God, and encourages us to give every part of our lives to His glory. Here are several ways to help us put this truth into practice in daily life:
a: Commitment in prayer
In daily prayer, give all glory to God, especially when we experience God’s rescue and protection. Actively ask God to help us avoid temptation and overcome evil.
Recognize God’s sovereignty
When you face decisions and challenges in life, recognize that all authority and kingdom are under God’s control. This will help us stay humble and depend on God’s wisdom and guidance.
Conduct that glorifies God
At work and in community interactions, glorify God through conduct. This includes treating others justly and setting an example in honesty and integrity.
Share God’s works
Share with others what God has done in your life, especially testimonies of redemption and changed lives. This not only glorifies God but also encourages and inspires others to seek Him.
A thankful attitude
Stay thankful for every blessing in life, big or small. A thankful attitude helps us recognize God’s hand and give glory to Him.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You, because the kingdom, the power, and the glory belong to You forever. Help us in daily life to follow Your will, be kept from temptation, and be delivered from evil. May our every action and decision reflect reverence and honor for You. Show Your glory in our hearts and lives. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength and peace in God’s kingdom and experience His boundless glory and protection. Amen!

v: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
b: This verse tells us that God’s glory lies in His wisdom and mystery, while humanity’s glory lies in the process of seeking and discovering truth. God, in His infinite wisdom and knowledge, has hidden many things, and we, as His people, have both the responsibility and the privilege to seek and understand these mysteries.

It is like a great explorer whose glory lies in his continual exploring of unknown realms, discovering new continents and treasures. In the same way, on our journey of faith, to keep seeking God’s truth and wisdom is itself a glory. God has hidden many mysteries in our lives, waiting for us to explore and discover them, a special grace and challenge that He has given us.

A young scientist had been full of curiosity about the universe since childhood. He spent countless nights under the stars trying to understand its mysteries. Years later he became an astronomer and discovered new galaxies and planets. Each time he made a discovery he felt immense excitement and honor, because he knew that these discoveries brought him closer to God’s wisdom and creation.

This story tells us that each of us, in our own field, through continual learning and exploring, can discover God’s mysteries and wisdom. Whether we are scientists, teachers, artists, or in any other profession, through our effort and wisdom we can display God’s glory.

Dear family, let us always keep a hunger for God’s wisdom and truth in life, and be bold to explore and learn, discovering the mysteries God has hidden in our lives. In this way we can not only understand and know God better but also display His glory in the process.
ah: Proverbs 25:2 encourages us to see that seeking truth and understanding is a wise act, reflecting the different glories of God and of kings. Here are concrete ways to put this verse into practice in daily life:
a: Seek wisdom
When you face decisions or difficulties, actively seek God’s wisdom and guidance, deepening your understanding of God’s will through prayer, Bible reading, and consulting spiritually mature friends.
Learn humbly
Do not be content with the knowledge you already have, but keep learning and seeking truth. This applies not only to spiritual growth but also to professional skills and everyday knowledge.
Transparency and honesty
Practice transparency and honesty in your personal and professional life. This is the foundation for respecting others and earning trust, and a concrete expression of “searching out a matter.”
Share knowledge and truth
Share what you have learned and understood with others, in church groups, at home, or in society, helping them grow and also glorifying God.
Prayer and reflection
Regularly take time to reflect on your conduct and motives, asking God to reveal any hidden pride or selfishness, and to give a humble heart that seeks His glory rather than personal glory.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the teaching of this verse, which reminds us that it is God’s glory to conceal a matter, and our task to search it out. Give us wisdom and courage to keep seeking truth in daily life, to live with transparency and honesty, and to use every day’s conduct to glorify You. Help us to be seekers of truth and spreaders of wisdom. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s infinite wisdom and love as you seek truth, and find your own glory on this journey. Amen!

v: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come before him. Worship the LORD in holy array.
b: This verse reminds us that we should give all glory to God and worship Him with pure and reverent hearts. God is worthy of all glory and praise, for He is the Lord who created all things. When we worship, we should bring not only an offering but also holy array, that is, worship Him with a pure heart and pure conduct.

It is like a carefully prepared wedding: the bride wears a white gown that symbolizes her hope for her new life and her love for the groom. We are the same before God, coming before Him with the purest hearts and conduct, as an expression of our love and reverence for Him.

A little girl always brought her favorite Bible with her when she went to Sunday school. The Bible was a gift from her grandmother and was filled with her grandmother’s blessings and prayers for her. Whenever she opened it, she felt her grandmother’s love and God’s presence. She understood that bringing this Bible to church was her worship of God and also her thanks to her grandmother.

This little girl’s story tells us that worshiping God is not merely outward form but sincerity and gratitude of heart. Whatever offering we bring before God, as long as our hearts are pure and reverent, God will accept our worship.
Dear family, let us always remember in life to give all glory to God and to worship Him with pure and reverent hearts. In this way our lives will be filled with God’s presence and blessing.
ah: 1 Chronicles 16:29 reminds us to honor God with fitting worship and offerings. Here are some concrete, practical ways to help us put this verse into practice in daily life:
a: Prepare your heart
Take time each day to quiet your heart, and through prayer and silence focus your heart on God, making worship part of daily life.
A holy life
Pursue holiness in personal conduct and speech, avoid everything that might defile the heart, and live a life consistent with God’s Word.
Giving and serving
Regularly give your time, talents, and possessions to the service of the church and community as an offering to God, expressing love and respect for God by action.
Holy array
“Holy array” here can be understood as outward and inward attitude, that is, coming before God with a humble and thankful heart, whether in church worship or in daily life.
Set up an altar to God at home
Set up a corner for prayer at home, as a reminder to yourself and your family to keep worshiping God in daily life.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us to honor You with holy lives and sincere worship. Help us to treat every day as an opportunity to give ourselves to You, showing love and service for You not only in the church but also in our homes and at work. May our lives be a witness to Your glory, and through our conduct give You the glory due to You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God’s glory and love in worship, and glorify Him with a holy heart and conduct. Amen!

v: “Worthy are you, our Lord and God, the Holy One, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, for you created all things, and because of your desire they existed and were created!”
b: This verse tells us that God is worthy of all glory, honor, and power, because He is the Lord who created all things. Whenever we see the beauty of nature and feel the miracle of life, we should praise God, because it was all created by Him.

It is like an artist who has created a great painting that displays his outstanding talent and boundless creativity. When we admire the painting, we cannot help praising the artist. In the same way, when we admire the world God created, seeing the grandeur of the sky, the vastness of the sea, and the fragrance of the flowers, we should praise and thank God, because it is all His masterpiece.

A farmer spent time every morning praying in his fields, thanking God for the fruitful land and his wonderful family. Although his life was not wealthy, his heart was full of gratitude and joy. This farmer knew that whatever difficulties he met in life, he could rely on God, because God is the Lord who created all things and will care for all his needs.
This story reminds us that whatever state our life is in, we should be thankful and praise God’s creation and grace, because He is the God worthy of all glory, honor, and power.
Dear family, let us give thanks and praise to God at all times in daily life, because He is the ruler who created all things. All we have is His gift, so let us honor His name with thankful hearts.
ah: Revelation 4:11 emphasizes the greatness of God’s creation of all things, and that all things exist because of His will. We can put this truth into practice in daily life in the following ways:
a: Know the greatness of the Creator
Spend time each day observing nature, whether a tree in a city park or the stars in the night sky, and reflect on the wonder and purpose of what God created.
Give thanks for everything in life
In daily prayer, thank God for every resource and opportunity He has given, including food, family, work, and friendships.
Respect all life

Respect and protect the life God created, including people, animals, and the natural environment, through practical action. This can be done by supporting sustainable products, reducing waste, and joining community clean-up activities.
Teach and share

For families with children, teach children about the mystery of creation and share our responsibility as God’s creatures. In church or in groups, share the importance of creation and how we can glorify God by our conduct.
Reflect on and practice God’s will
In personal decisions and life choices, seek what is in line with God’s will. This involves praying for guidance and making sure our conduct reflects honor and obedience to God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for creating the whole universe, and for giving all glory, honor, and power to the Lord we know. Help us, through every choice and every action in daily life, to show respect and thanks to You. Make us witnesses of Your glory, showing Your love and authority among people. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you sense God’s creation and love every day of your life, and glorify Him with a thankful heart. Amen!

v: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory—
b: This verse tells us that God has a great plan: to make known the riches of His glory on us, who are vessels of mercy. Each of us is a vessel that God has specially prepared, and He wants to show His glory and mercy in our lives.

It is like a potter who carefully shapes each vessel, and each vessel has its own unique design and use. In the same way, God designs each of our lives with care. He knows our strengths and weaknesses, and He is preparing us to be witnesses of His glory.

A man who had been unemployed for years, in extreme poverty, still firmly believed in God’s promises. Every day he eagerly helped people in need and kept giving thanks for God’s grace. Later he found a job at a charity, helping homeless people.
